articleTitle: Exploring MTPA Technique in Field-Oriented Control of IPMSM Drive for Enhancing Efficiency of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Electric vehicles have gained significant traction as a sustainable alternative to traditional combustion engine vehicles. However, enhancing their efficiency remains a paramount challenge for widespread adoption. This paper focuses on applying Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) technology in Field-Oriented Control (FOC) of IPMSM Drives to augment the efficiency of EVs. The MTPA Technique aims to fine-tune motor efficiency by regulating the current supplied. In the context of EVs, the key components are the IPMSM motor and battery bank, whose specifications are determined based on calculations of total load, required torque, aerodynamic drag, grading resistance, and rolling resistance. Performance evaluation is conducted using MATLAB/Simulink, assessing parameters like Speed vs Time, Current vs Time, Torque vs Time, and KWH vs Time. The paper aims to advance EV technology by providing a comprehensive methodology for increasing efficiency, thereby facilitating the transition to sustainable transportation solutions.

articleTitle: A Review on Grid-Connected SPV Systems in India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Global energy demand has increased significantly owing to technical advancements, fast industrial expansion, and rising home energy use. This prompted engineers and planners to explore methods for harnessing alternate energy sources beyond fossil fuels. Solar, wind, biomass, and micro hydro are among the resources used globally for energy generation, contingent upon resource availability. The notion of integrating solar electricity into the utility grid has gained significant popularity in the current age of renewable energy production and delivery. Hence, this paper gives an overview of the performance study of grid-connected SPV systems in India. Moreover, this paper also presents the upto date bibliography which will be benefited to those who are doing in this area of research.

articleTitle: AlexResNet+: Enhancing Breast Cancer Detection through Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The area of machine learning that uses deep neural networks (DNNs) is called deep learning. Current developments in device learning with larger and deeper representation strategies are using a "cease-to-cease" instructional strategy, deep learning approaches and expand a deep learning set of protocols and methodologies that may accurately detect the majority of breast cancers during mammography screening. An efficient training method makes use of training datasets that either include the complete scientific annotation or only the most tumors found (tagged) throughout the image. According to deep learning, there are at least three or four layers, with the input layers leading to the output layers. A Deep Hybrid Featured Machine Learning Model for Classifying Breast Cancer Tissue is called AlexResNet+. We used the well-liked and incredibly successful deep learning models, AlexNet and ResNet101, for deep feature extraction. To achieve optimal computing efficiency while preserving high dimensional deep features, we employed AlexNet, which consists of three fully connected layers and five convolutional layers. In contrast, ResNet101 was used with modified layered structures. We combined the feature set and used it as input for the radial basis function support vector machine (SVM-RBF). which is employed in two-class classification, after extracting the distinctive deep features from the deep learning models of AlexNet and ResNet.To evaluate the effectiveness of the different feature sets, distinct performances for AlexNet, short for ResNet101, and hybrid features were obtained.

articleTitle: A Comparative analysis of various segmentation techniques for breast thermal images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the deadliest diseases among women ranging from young to old and second common disease that leads to death for women after lung cancer. In this paper investigates the effectiveness of thresholding, edge detection, region-based, and watershed-based segmentation techniques on breast thermal images captured from five distinct perspectives: front view, left at 45°, left at 90°, right at 45° and right at 90° views. The main objective of this research is to identify an appropriate segmentation technique that can improve the accuracy of breast cancer detection in noninvasively through thermal imaging. Each segmentation technique is applied on Region of Interest (ROI) breast thermal images to accurately delineate the breast abnormalities. Results suggest a suitable segmentation that is suitable to analyze breast thermal images with particular angle.

articleTitle: Characteristics Investigation of Dual Rotor Single Stator 6-Phase Single I-Shaped Magnetic Pole PMSM for Smart Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This paper investigates the characteristics of a Dual Rotor Single Stator 6-Phase Single I-Shaped Magnetic Pole PMSM (DRSSSPSISMP-PMSM) designed for smart electric vehicle (EV) applications. The motor arrangement is designed to enhance the efficiency, power density, and performance of electric vehicle (EV) propulsion systems. Its distinctive design features two rotors, one stator, and a multi-phase operation, which collectively maximize torque production and improve operational reliability. To assess critical performance like electromagnetic torque, torque vs speed, power vs speed and % efficiency vs load current characteristics, an electromagnetic analysis using Finite Element Method (FEM) is performed. Additionally, transient analysis is used in this work to evaluate the dynamic behavior under various operating situations. The findings imply that the suggested motor is more suited for applications involving smart electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Classification of Power Quality Disturbances Using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Power quality disturbances such as voltage sags, swells, harmonics, and transients pose significant challenges to electrical systems. To address these issues, this study employs the Fourier Synchro Squeezing Transform (FSST) for preprocessing various power quality signals, enhancing the accuracy of the analysis. The research focuses on classifying these disturbances using four prominent machine learning algorithms: Support Vector Machine 91% accuracy (SVM), Random Forest 96% accuracy (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine 99% accuracy (GBM), and Logistic Regression 90% accuracy (LR). The Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) demonstrates superior performance due to its iterative process, achieving the highest classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Behavior of a 10kVA Single-Phase Dry Transformer Under Diverse Lightning Impulses: A Simulation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation-based model of a 10 kVA, 33 kV/415 V, single-phase dry transformer subjected to standard as well as non-standard lightning impulse voltages. The analysis of the transformer's subsequent responses is then described. Dry-type transformers are known for their safety, low maintenance requirements, lack of pollution, ease of installation, environmental friendliness, and fire protection features. However, non-standard lightning impulse voltages can have a detrimental impact on electrical insulation. For this reason, electrical equipment typically undergoes a lightning impulse voltage test using a standardized waveform (1.2 × 50 μs) after manufacturing. Recognizing that real-world lightning strikes often deviate from this standard waveform, a simulation model of a real-life 10 kVA, 33 kV/415 V single-phase dry transformer was developed to understand the behaviour of insulation under non-standard impulse voltages. This model was then used to analyze the transformer's response to both standard (SLI) and non-standard lightning impulse (NSLI) waveforms.

articleTitle: Improve System Voltage Stability and Reduction in Losses with Optimal Placement of DG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Growing load demand on the distribution system draws focus to the active distribution system. in the active distribution system distribution generation (DG) is emerging as a viable alternative to the increasingly depleting traditional energy supplies. With the use of Distributed Generation in a distribution system has a significant effect to reduce the line loss and improvement in the voltage profile. This work proposes an approach to optimize the voltage profile and reduce overall line loss in the distribution system by optimally placement and size of distributed generator. The optimization issue is stated by considering the line losses and voltage profile of the distribution system. The utilization of a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) based methodology is used to ascertain the most effective solution. Additionally, the backward forward load flow technique is employed to study the power flow in a distribution system. The proposed method is evaluated on an IEEE-12 bus radial distribution system, and the simulation results are shown to demonstrate the effectiveness of the recommended approach.

articleTitle: A PUF based Authentication Technique for IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) have grown tremendously in last few decades due to the availability and low cost of Internet and sensors. The authentication of these large numbers of IoT devices is very important and has security concern since they are mainly deployed in open insecure environment. Also, the security technology that is being used by the existing severs cannot be applied to them since they operate with limited processor, memory and power and they only operate with lightweight or minimal security functions making them vulnerable for many security incidents also traditional authentication process mainly focuses on device to server authentication. Hence a novel device to device authentication scheme for IoT devices using Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) have been proposed which provides mutual authentication between IoT devices where authentication server acts as a reliable intermediary. Various security analysis has been discussed which can be defended by using proposed method.

articleTitle: Power Flow and Performance Analysis of Three Port Converter in Street Light
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This research presents design and implementation of a stand-alone solar-powered street lighting system, featuring a Three port converter (TPC) circuit. The system, which incorporates a photovoltaic (PV) source and battery storage is designed to ensure consistent power delivery. The converter operates in two distinct modes: buck mode charges the battery during daylight, while boost mode powers the LED at night. Controlled via Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) signals, the converter facilitates efficient and reliable bidirectional power flow. Simulation and experimental data highlight the system’s effectiveness, confirming its operational efficiency and theoretical design.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of V/F Control for Solar Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The paper provides a comprehensive study on the design and implementation of scalar control for a Standalone Solar Water Pumping System. The induction motor of 3HP is considered in this proposed system. It covered the entire system from solar panel power extraction using a boost converter with P &O MPPT algorithm to controlling an induction motor using scalar control via an inverter. The boost converter operated at a switching frequency of 18 kHz, while the inverter operated at 15 kHz. The performance of scalar control in various speed variation scenarios is thoroughly analyzed using MATLAB Simulink simulations, and the results are validated through hardware implementation. This approach ensures the effectiveness and reliability of the SWPS in rural environments with limited or no grid connectivity.

articleTitle: Closing the Supply Chain Circularity Gap with Block Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: A circular supply chain refers to a sustainable business model that aims to reduce waste and promote resource efficiency throughout the entire lifecycle of a product. Globally, supply chains are being transformed to support circularity through the adoption of technology like blockchain. With the real-time data-sharing capabilities of Blockchain (BC), unparalleled visibility, instant reporting, and priceless insights can be used to trigger circular behaviors in supply chains. Because of these reasons, BC has become a critical technology solution for creating sustainable, circular, and transparent supply chains for industries. However, the building blocks of BC may not be efficiently implemented in all the functions of the supply chain because of the complexities faced by the stakeholders at different levels. This study aims to identify BC's circular building blocks (CBB) for the circular supply chain (CSC). Further, the study investigates supply chain functions that can quickly adopt blockchain. It is found that BC adoption is more significant in procurement, manufacturing, and remanufacturing functions as the circularity of the supply chain is more prominent in these functions.

articleTitle: Prediction And Classification Of Glaucoma Disease Through GAN Based Efficient Deep Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In modern days Glaucoma is become a disease that make impact on matter of visions for human eyesight. This is an irreversible disease where vision difficulties will be outcomes. Now ML oriented Learning models based framework is created for the proper identifying of glaucoma. So purpose of particular work of making a Computer Aided Diagnostic System may perform faster detection and diagnosis as well as providing quicker treatment to patients. So the framework is created for detection of glaucoma using CNN and ML based approaches using SVM model on augmented datasets. The classes of diseases are classified as glaucoma and non-glaucoma found out for this jobs. Here CNN is required for Image Classification of Glaucoma Positive or Glaucoma Negative, cases. So the use of manual image processing methods or human intervention based methods are not needed here . Here medical image segmentation, AI and ML based approach is used for performing medical diagnosis more accurately. So CNN based Deep neural network are giving more than 90% of accuracy of efficiently classifying the diseases. Here data augmentation provides a significant roles of generation of several more new images that are very much useful for this research work for effective disease identification system. Also our created model gives more than 90% of train/validation/test accuracy score for classification of augmented datasets for AI based GAN network of creating higher resolution images.

articleTitle: Advancing Sustainable Manufacturing with IoT and Deep Reinforcement Learning in the Industry 4.0 Era
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)

authors.preferredName: P N V Syamala Rao M

abstract: Nowadays with the emergence of Industry 4. 0, there is therefore the need to have sustainable manufacturing in order to increase operational efficiency as well as relieve the pressure on the environment. A potential weakness of conventional approaches is time-dependency while processing real-time data to prevent dysfunctions in the company’s resource management, energy consumption control, and predictive maintenance. Thus, in this work it is proposed an innovative approach to address these problems with the use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Internet of Things (IoT) technology. Energy consumption, machine performance and environmental data are collected by IoT sensors in real-time and fed into a DRL model. This concept effectively eliminates the vices that are characteristic of conventional approaches in that it seeks to optimize production processes by cell design. The approach suggested above attains an unprecedented 98. 2% accuracy rate. This is in a bid to exemplify its capability in predicting these phenomenal and balance forecasts, to improve the overall performance and sustainability of manufacturing. Thereby, the method offers a robust answer to the acute questions arising in front-line manufacturing today and sets a brand-new reference for intelligent and sustainable behavior in the context of the fourth industrial revolution 4.0.

articleTitle: Interoperability Analysis of Charging Coils for Wireless Charging of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This study explores the optimization of wireless charging systems for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) through an analysis of planar coil geometries' interoperability. By examining Bipolar (BP) coils as transmitters and circular, double D (DD), and BP coils as receivers, the research aims to determine optimal coil pairings. Since multi-coil geometries such as BP and DD coil can be excited in various ways, interoperability analysis was performed between transmitter and receiver coil for all possible excitation mode. Results highlight the superiority of BP coils as transmitters, particularly in their compatibility with circular and DD receivers across various excitation modes. Single coil excitation emerges as promising, demonstrating favorable coupling and misalignment tolerance with circular receivers. This research underscores the importance of interoperability analysis in enhancing wireless charging efficiency for UAVs. Future endeavors will focus on further refining coil designs and developing comprehensive chargers with enhanced misalignment tolerance, thereby advancing drone technology capabilities.

articleTitle: A comparative study of dual-SC and dual-MRC over SBX fading channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The signals in wireless communication channel are impacted by different types of fading during a transmission. One of the ways to tackle the ill-effects of multipath fading is by using diversity method. This paper evaluates dual- selection combining (SC) diversity and dual-maximal ratio combining (MRC) diversity through Shadowed Beaulieu-Xie (SBX). SBX is a composite model which characterizes a communication environment consisting of line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight signals components together. A comparative study has been conducted in respect of outage probability and average bit error rate for dual-SC and dual-MRC over SBX fading channel. The consequences of fading and shadowing parameters on the system performances are also considered. The results are analytically obtained and validated using Monte-Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: Improving the Load Frequency Control of a Renewable Energy Penetrated Dual Area Power System with a 2DOFPID Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This paper implemented the territory control strategy to obtain an improvement in the load frequency control (LFC) performance of a dual area renewable energy power system (DAREPS). Initially, the DAREPS is laid with 10% step load disturbance (SLD), and the system behavior is studied under the supervision of the water cycle algorithm (WCA)-based two-degree-of-freedom proportional-integral-derivative (2DOFPID) controller. The performance efficacy of the 2DOFPID controller at the secondary level is demonstrated with the other available controllers. However, the DAREPS is considered with realistic constraints to get the investigation closer to the practical environment. Later, the DAREPS behavior is studied with the integration of the superconducting magnetic energy storage devices (SMES) in the control regions and the placement of the unified power flow controller (UPFC) with the tie-line. Simulation analysis revealed the enrichment in DAREPS performance with the implementation of the SMES-UPFC strategy.

articleTitle: Cloud Quantum Resource Allocation using Game Theoretic Quantum Based Dynamic Combinatorial Auction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Resource allocation in cloud quantum computing environments is a challenging problem due to the combinatorial nature of quantum resources and the strategic behavior of users. This paper presents a novel Game Theoretic Quantum Dynamic Combinatorial Auction (GTQBDCA) framework for efficient and fair allocation of quantum resources in cloud environments. By integrating game theory and dynamic combinatorial auctions, our approach addresses the unique challenges of quantum resource allocation, ensuring optimal resource utilization and user satisfaction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework through theoretical analysis and simulation results.

articleTitle: Adaptive MPPT with Integrated PSO-Tuned ANFIS Method for Optimal Performance in Grid-Connected PV Systems Using Hybrid PSO-ANN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In this research, we focus on increasing the power produced by solar panels under various environmental conditions. To optimize efficiency, we employ an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique. This method leverages the strengths of both fuzzy logic and neural networks to enhance tracking accuracy. To further improve the adaptability and performance of the controller, we utilize Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to tune its parameters. This tuning process allows the controller to dynamically adjust to changing environmental conditions, making it more effective in real-world applications. By integrating PSO with ANFIS, our goal is to enhance the precision of tracking the maximum power point and enable the system to respond swiftly to variations in solar radiation. We conducted performance evaluations using simulations and compared the results with those obtained from existing MPPT methods. The findings indicate that our proposed technique efficiently generates electricity in grid-connected solar systems. This research makes a significant contribution to the field of renewable energy by presenting a smart and flexible approach to harnessing solar energy. The combination of PSO and ANFIS not only improves the efficiency of solar power generation but also ensures that the system can adapt to diverse and dynamic environmental conditions. As a result, this technique offers a promising solution for enhancing the performance and reliability of solar power systems, thereby supporting the broader adoption and integration of renewable energy sources into the grid.

articleTitle: A Cloud Based Predictive and Preventive Maintenance for Electric Vehicle Fleet Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In today’s transportation and logistics industry, fleet management has become a critical success factor for businesses across industries. A Fleet Management System (FMS) stands as a comprehensive solution designed to simplify the complex processes of vehicle or asset management. This paper explains the critical role of FMS in optimizing fleet operations, improving productivity, and ensuring compliance. By providing an integral set of tools and functions, FMS empowers fleet managers to provide real-time visibility, operational insight, and control of their fleet, ultimately resulting in cost savings, improved security, and controls. This paper discusses the storage of sensor data and prediction of battery parameters using Hybrid machine learning technique LSTM-MLP which is a combination of both LSTM and MLP ML techniques to resolve the shortcomings of the individual ML methods leading to desired results.

articleTitle: PV, Wind, Battery integrated UPQC system Performance with PI, Fuzzy and ANFIS controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This research paper investigates the performance of a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) system integrated with photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind energy, and battery storage, using three distinct control strategies: Proportional-Integral (PI), Fuzzy Logic, and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controllers. The integration of renewable energy sources with battery storage into the UPQC aims to enhance power quality and system reliability in the presence of grid disturbances such as voltage sags, swells, and harmonics. The study begins by modeling the PV, wind, and battery components, followed by the implementation of the UPQC system. Each controller is then applied to the system, and its performance is evaluated based on metrics such as Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), voltage regulation during disturbances, and the speed of system response. Simulation results indicate that while the PI controller offers satisfactory performance under stable conditions, it struggles with rapid changes in load and supply. In contrast, the Fuzzy Logic controller demonstrates improved adaptability and robustness, particularly in handling non-linearities. However, the ANFIS controller outperforms both PI and Fuzzy controllers by combining the benefits of adaptive learning and fuzzy logic, resulting in superior power quality improvement and faster settling times during grid disturbances. This paper concludes that the ANFIS controller is the most effective in managing the complexities of a PV, wind, and battery-integrated UPQC system, offering significant advantages in both power quality enhancement and system resilience.

articleTitle: Non Destructive Testing For Differentiating Rhode Island Red and White Leghorn Chicken Egg Breeds Using Hyperspectral Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The Process of Grading and Segregation of chicken eggs in various breeds plays a Vital role to assess the standards of eggs that can enable the market to provide Quality eggs to the consumers. The current traditional grading mechanisms are manual and carried on observable traits like shell color and form, that are prone to human mistakes. These manual methods not only make the process cumbersome, but also raises the management cost. To overcome these challenges, this research aimed to differentiate Rhode Island red and white leghorn chicken eggs using non-destructive hyperspectral imaging techniques. Unlike manual inspection or invasive tagging, a nondestructive hyperspectral imaging setup captures a wide range of spectral information from chicken eggs, identifying minor differences in color and texture among different egg breeds in poultry farming. In this experiment, a sample set of 72 Rhode Island red and 72 white leghorn chicken eggs has been tested by using hyperspectral imaging. Spectral features of each breed say Rhode Island red and white leghorn chicken eggs have been identified to differentiate both the breeds.

Author Keywords: white leghorn and Rhode Island red

articleTitle: Geometrical pole shape optimization of an outer rotor synchronous reluctance motor for output torque enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This article explores optimizing design for Permanent magnet (PM) free outer rotor synchronous reluctance machines to be used as in-wheel motors for electric vehicles. The primary objective is enhancing torque output by systematically analyzing various rotor pole shapes and parameters such as pole depth, arc angles, rib thickness, channel width, and fillet radii. These parameters were studied on four different types of pole shapes. Using ANSYS Maxwell software, the analysis is performed on an outer rotor motor with a diameter of 190 mm and a rated speed of 1200 RPM. The results indicate that outer rotor machines with configurations such as an inner arc angle of 9 degrees and an outer arc angle of 24 degrees exhibit optimal torque output for pole shape 1. Moreover, the study reveals that an increase in pole depth (SB) corresponds to an increase in torque output, while rib thickness reduces torque output. Additionally, the research explores the impact of fillet radii on torque performance. This study provides the effects of essential features of critical design parameters on reluctance torque for maximizing average torque in outer rotor motors utilized in EV applications.

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Optimization based 2DOF-PID Controller for Load Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This work introduces a novel Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) tuned two-degree-of-freedom proportional-integral-derivative (2DOF-PID) controller for load frequency control (LFC). LFC involves a set of control mechanisms that adjust the output of power generation units in response to changes in load and generation. Several modern techniques are applied to implement a stabilizing controller. An analysis of the dynamic performance of LFC using optimization method and the LFC problem in a power system with two power generating units has been established. In order to suppress oscillation, a 2DOF-PID control method is proposed in this study. The best controller parameters are found by applying recently developed algorithms. The controller performances are analysed by using the MATLAB/SIMULINK tool.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of Lithium-ion battery for Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The thermal behavior of energy storage systems, mainly lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries, is vital for electric vehicle (EV) applications. This study provides a thermal analysis of Li-ion batteries at 0°C, 25°C, 50°C, and 75°C, focusing on both core and surface temperatures to underscore the importance of effective thermal management. Using a Matlab/Simulink model, the temperature change concerning the core and surface was calculated. The results show that the core heats up more than the surface due to internal reactions and energy losses, creating a temperature gradient. If the core temperature exceeds safe limits, it can result in risks like thermal runaway. These findings emphasize the need for advanced thermal management systems specifically designed for Li-ion batteries in EVs.

articleTitle: A Lossless Grounded/Floating Active Inductor Employing Single DV-DXCCTA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In this paper, a new lossless grounded and floating active inductance simulator by employing a single Differential Voltage Dual – X Current Conveyor Transconductance Amplifier (DV-DXCCTA) active element and an external grounded capacitor is introduced. The presented inductance simulator utilizes two transconductance parameters (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m1</inf>, g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m2</inf>) for the electronically tunable nature of the proposed inductor. The functionality test of the proposed simulator circuits is verified using 0.18 μm TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company) CMOS technology parameter and experimental verification with the help of traditional ICs specially Current Feedback Operational Amplifier (CFOA) as AD844 and Operational Transconductance Amplifier (OTA) as CA3080 for DV-DXCCTA realization. Some useful signal processing applications viz. Single Input Triple Output (SITO) filter, and higher-order low-pass filter are critically examined by using the proposed inductor.

articleTitle: Training Analysis of Optimizers on Flood Object Dataset using EfficientNetB0 - A Novel Deep Learning Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Urban flooding is an escalating global challenge, exacerbated by rapid city growth and climate change. These inundations cause widespread economic damage, pose health hazards, and disrupt critical infrastructure. While deep learning has proven effective in various predictive tasks, its application to flood forecasting remains limited. The performance of these models hinges on their training process, optimization techniques, and the number of learning iterations. This study aims to enhance urban flood resilience. It focuses on evaluating the EfficientNetB0 model's performance using three optimization algorithms: ADAM, SDGM, and RMSPROP. The research assesses each optimizer's efficacy by varying the number of epochs while maintaining other hyperparameters constant. Notably, when applied to object detection in the training dataset, the model achieves an outstanding 100% success rate using the ADAM optimizer.

articleTitle: Design and monitoring of 36V 7.5AH Lithium-ion Battery Pack for Electric Bi-cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The demand for efficient and reliable energy storage systems has seen a significant surge with the increasing adoption of electric vehicles, renewable energy sources, and portable electronic devices. The faults occurring batteries of these vehicles are also increasing. This paper focuses on the comprehensive design and monitoring aspects of a battery pack to address the challenges associated with maximizing performance, ensuring safety, and prolonging the overall lifespan of the battery system. The design phase involves the selection and integration of individual battery cells, considering factors such as energy density, power density, thermal management, and overall pack architecture. The paper explores temperature monitoring (DS18B20), Speed monitoring (Hall sensor), and voltage monitoring to optimize the overall efficiency, stores the data in a memory card with help of SD card module and prevent issues like thermal runaway and capacity fade. The NRF24L01 wireless transmission module and the NEO-6M GPS module may work together to effectively track the location of a bicycle. When combined, these devices allow the bicycle's location to be tracked in real time. Location data is gathered by the NEO-6M GPS module and wirelessly sent via the NRF24L01 module. Applications like as bicycle route tracking, theft prevention, and bicycle usage monitoring for logistical or fitness reasons are where this system works.

articleTitle: PWM-Controlled AC-AC Boost Converter for Domestic Induction Heating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This research explores the application of an innovative AC-AC Boost Converter for domestic induction heating, employing precise control through Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) control. The proposed system aims to enhance the efficiency and controllability of induction heating processes commonly employed in household applications. The AC-AC Boost Converter provides a foundation for improved power delivery, optimizing energy transfer. The incorporation of PWM control adds a layer of precision to the system, allowing for accurate modulation of the inverter parameters to meet specific heating requirements. The study employs PSIM simulation tool to analyze the performance of the proposed system, considering factors such as power efficiency and overall system stability. Preliminary results indicate promising advancements in domestic induction heating technology, showcasing the potential for energy-efficient and adaptable solutions in household applications.

articleTitle: Induction Motor Drive for Low Cost EV with Improved Performance using A Three-Level VSC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The cost of an electric vehicle (EV) mostly covers the drive motor and battery. This paper presents use of an induction motor (IM) for EV fed through a three-level voltage source converter (VSC) with v/f control. The three-level VSC facilitates switch stress reduction while v/f control gives reduced control burden and simplest algorithm to implement. The proposed control concept is validated on a laboratory hardware setup under the extra urban driving cycle (EUDC). An EUDC is one of the most used driving cycles which reflects the aggressive behavior of drive cycle applied to an EV with high-speed driving modes. The complete control scheme is designed using real time interface blocks of MATLAB Simulink and implemented through dSPACE CLP 1104. The experimental performance results of IM drive with v/f control under EUDC are recorded on a digital storage oscilloscope and presented for validation of effective and improved performance of complete IM-based EV drive system.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Prophet model for application in Agro-Industry to forecast Pesticide consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Forecasting plays a key role in several industries to predict the probable requirement of a certain product or service over a period of time. This may or may not be dependent on certain external factors depending upon which, a suitable method needs to be chosen to perform the forecasting task. For a given data distribution, the best-fit model needs to be figured out after fine-tuning its hyperparameters to acquire the most optimal forecasts. In this paper, we have used the Prophet model of Facebook, an additive regression model to forecast the requirement of pesticides to be used for agricultural needs, and presented an overview of how fine-tuning the parameters leads to optimal curve fits, hence resulting in better-quality forecasts. We have also studied the impact of the size of the train data on the overall quality of predictions. Hence after combining both the data size and parameter values, the curve fits and predictions have been visually illustrated.

articleTitle: Investigation of Magnet Materials for In-Wheel BLDC Motors for Low-power Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The BLDC in-wheel motors are increasingly preferred for low-power electric vehicle applications due to their highly efficient mechanical energy conversion, high torque, and low maintenance compared to conventional BLDC motors. Additionally, they offer smooth operation, regenerative braking, and easy speed control. However, a key challenge in designing the rotor structure for in-wheel motors is managing heat, which can affect efficiency, and reliability, and lead to premature issues. This paper analyses three different magnet material analyses aimed at minimising losses and improving performances. These techniques include neodymium ferrite boron (NdFeB), samarium cobalt (SmCo), aluminium nickel cobalt (AlNiCo)and ferrite (Fe) material. A finite element model is employed to analyze motor solve software and study characteristics such as cogging torque, efficiency, speed-torque curve and magnetic field strength. Simulation results demonstrate that the exterior rotor with NdFeB magnet material enhances performance to meet the requirements for low-power electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Leveraging Gradient Boosting for Crime Prediction: A Focus on Women's Safety in India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In India, crimes against women is a concerning issue where incidents of rape, domestic violence etc are increasing at a very alarming rate. So predicting crime rates especially among women has become very critical. The data that is gathered from various crime incidents can be collected and preprocessed to further train models which can predict crime rates in advance. In this research paper, we used Gradient Boosting Regressor to analyze crime data. This data is further used to train our machine learning model. The purpose of our study is to evaluate the Gradient Boosting Regressor's effectiveness and performance in predicting different kinds of criminal incidents. Our model predicts a range of criminal activities, such as sexual assault, deaths related to dowries, abuse by spouses or their family members, kidnapping and abduction, insulting women's modesty, and the importation of girls. Our model demonstrated high predictive performance, with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values above 0.99 for most crime categories, indicating its ability to explain the majority of the variance in crime rates effectively. The model's robustness was confirmed by low MAE and MSE values, along with consistent cross-validated MSE, suggesting its generalizability to unseen data. The findings show how advanced algorithms based on ML can be used to analyse crime data and provide a reliable method for identifying and predicting patterns in criminal activity.

articleTitle: Voltage Mode All-Pass Filter Employing Single FTFNTA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This paper introduces a new single element block based First-Order Voltage Mode All-Pass Filter (VM-APF) circuit. The presented VM-APF circuit utilized single Four Terminal Floating Nullor Transconductance Amplifier (FTFNTA) active element, one floating capacitor, and one grounded MOS resistor. The simulation results are carried out using 0.18μm CMOS TSMC parameter. The topology can be tunable through bias current of FTFNTA and power consumption also very less. The theoretical approach are verified by simulation results. Monte Carlo Analysis (MCA) with 10% tolerance of capacitor as well as resistor for 100 runs in Guassian distribution is also perform. Experimental setup is also carried out using commercially available ICs like as CFOA (AD844) and OTA (CA3080) which validated the theoretical approach and simulation results.

articleTitle: THIPWM Based Three Level ANPC Converter for Bidirectional EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The electric vehicle (EV) sector is experiencing rapid growth, driven by global environmental concerns and the push for cleaner transportation. Converters are critical components in EV applications, with the challenge of selecting efficient topologies that maintain high performance under various load conditions. While traditional 2-level inverters and boost converters dominate, their efficiency decreases significantly under low-load conditions. Recent advancements have introduced transformerless grid-connected inverters, improving efficiency, yet issues such as common-mode voltage and ground leakage currents affect power quality.This paper presents the use of a three-level Active Neutral Point Clamped (3L-ANPC) converter for bidirectional EV charging applications, employing Third Harmonic Injection Pulse Width Modulation (THIPWM) for enhanced DC-link utilization and efficiency. Simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink, corroborated by experimental data, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in reducing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and improving power conversion efficiency.

Author Keywords: Third Harmonic Injection Pulse Width Modulation

articleTitle: A comprehensive approach for ranking of Solar power plants using hybrid MEREC-G and WISP in India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The selection of a site is an important task in the construction of a solar photovoltaic power plant, as countries are transitioning to renewable energy sources and not every location is suited for producing solar energy. The possible explanations for this can be encapsulated as the decrease in the availability of fossil fuels and the increase in pollution and the implementation of an evaluation model to ascertain the best place to build a solar power plant. Weighted criteria are implemented after restricted regions are excluded to generate the required calculation. Given that renewable energy sources are both environmentally benign and cost-effective, it is logical for countries with significant solar energy potential, such as India, to prioritize solar energy as a renewable energy source in their energy policies. The implementation of MCDM in this paper for choosing locations for solar power plants in India is done by identifying twenty-one impact factors. MEREC-G is employed to weight impact factors, which are subsequently ranked using the WISP method.

articleTitle: DFIG-based wind-driven system stability analysis for varying line reactance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The following paper provides a detailed examination of the modal analysis of a grid-connected doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG). The study aims to identify and analyze the inherent oscillating modes exhibited by the DFIG utilizing the single-machine infinite bus power system model. Furthermore, the research delves into an investigation of the impact of grid strength, particularly about varying line reactance. It also highlighted the effect of different line reactance particularly high line reactance on stator.

articleTitle: Design and Transformation of IC Engine Motorcycle into Hybrid Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In today's world, the escalating levels of pollution, largely propelled by carbon emissions, pose significant challenges to the environment. Ground-level atmosphere degradation and environmental impacts are evident consequences. However, hybrid vehicles emerge as promising solutions, offering a means to curb greenhouse gas emissions and reduce reliance on fossil fuels, thus potentially mitigating climate change. This paper delves into the operational mechanisms of hybrid vehicles, emphasizing the role of smart power management systems. These systems adeptly balance the utilization of internal combustion engines and electric motors, effectively minimizing pollution and optimizing fuel economy. Furthermore, the paper explores the recent advancements in battery technologies, crucial for enhancing the overall efficiency and performance of ICE engine with hybrid mode compared for economic benefit for a customer hence enable superior energy storage capabilities, facilitating seamless operation and yielding improved fuel efficiency and reduced emissions.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Detecting Skin Diseases Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The fact that the skin is the outermost layer of the body means that skin illnesses are widespread. Preventing these conditions from becoming life-threatening requires early detection. Thus, academics are now concentrating a great deal of effort on deep learning methods for diagnosing skin conditions. This paper looks at the different ways that scientists are trying to identify skin illnesses using deep learning technologies. We provide a succinct introduction to skin diseases, including information on datasets, kinds, and data preprocessing methods. We also discuss the deep learning paradigm and describe popular deep learning techniques used to diagnose skin diseases. Presenting a thorough literature overview of current studies on deep learning approaches for skin disease diagnosis is the main goal of this work. Our results show that deep learning approaches surpass dermatologists, different machine-based treatment plans, and other classification techniques in the identification of skin diseases from images due to their high accuracy.

articleTitle: Boosting Power Systems Resilience Against Counterfeiting Of GPS Attacks Using Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Cyber security concerns have been brought up by the expanding usage of wireless technology in power systems, notably regarding GPS counterfeiting attacks (GCAs). Phasor measurement units (PMUs) experience phase angle adjustments as a result of these attacks, which distort GPS data. This work proposes a Deep-learning GPS-Spoofing Counteraction (DLGSC) algorithm that uses PMU data for PMU measurement correction and GCA identification. For signal rectification after the identification of attacks, the proposed technique separately uses an assortment of long short-term memory (LSTM) units and a recurrent neural network (RNN). In contrast with conventional approaches, which either cannot handle concurrent attacks or static, DLGSC addresses these issues by utilizing deep learning methodologies. DLGSC obtains precise results by choosing suitable features for GCA identification. Thereafter total least square-estimation of signal parameters via the rotational invariance technique (TLS-ESPRIT) is used for the modal estimation. The efficacy & resilience of the proposed technique is confirmed and contrasted with other recently discovered methods. Additionally, real probing data, local area data, and two area data from the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) are used to validate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Reinforced Multilingual Geospatial Query Extraction Using Naive Bayes and Fuzzy Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The paper introduces a method for automatic canonicalization of geospatial entities from an unstructured language input given by the user. The traditional and old method of Geospatial canonical search is outdated and has loopholes for the handling of the multilingual input and most importantly the accuracy of the model. The system is designed to handle Textual input and Voice Modulated input. To detect and correct the non- standardized geospatial entities, which includes those with typographical errors or unconventional spellings, we use the advanced natural language processing (NLP) technique for standardizing the entities. By using the custom Naive Bayes probability algorithm, the Model identifies potential geospatial entities by recognizing the incorrectly spelled names and matching them with their correct form using the naive bayes probability algorithm. Furthermore, to enhance the identification of entities accuracy we use the system which has some per-defined list of abbreviations for geographical features like (mountains, lakes, oceans etc.) In case the where the same place name exists in multiple locations in same or different country (like Punjab in both India and Pakistan), then the Model provides the geographical output data for all the relevant locations with their exact longitude and latitude coordinates. After this the model triggers the fuzzy matching algorithm which uses the token ratio technique to ensure the precise mapping of corrected names to their canonical forms in the dataset.

articleTitle: Classification of Gait in Children Suffering from Cerebral Palsy using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Classification of abnormal walking patterns are required for developing customised therapies for children with cerebral palsy (CP). Hip, ankle, and knee joint angles calculated with respect to sagittal and coronal planes are used in the proposed work to evaluate a number of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models. The main goal is to assess how well various algorithms work on abnormal gait data, where the data has been improved by converting time series data into heatmap images and using methods like zooming and rotation on converted images to increase model robustness. The augmented gait data is classified using seven different models: Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), k-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) and ResNet. The CNN model achieved the highest classification accuracy of 86.26

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a DC-Fast Charging System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: With recent advancement in EVs and requirement for more adoption of EVs, the charging infrastructure development and technology development are the main focus. The problems, customers faced on using with electric vehicles are mostly on taking too much time on charging the vehicles that can be solved by developing a fast-charger. In this paper, the issues related to the charging time of electric vehicles and the problems that comes with it, and the topologies on making a fast charger for electric vehicles is studied. A DC fast charging system is designed and simulated using MATLAB Simulink software and the results are discussed about making a feasible fast-charger that can operate bidirectional. This can be used to charge the battery from the grid when power is required by the EV battery and excess energy from the battery of the EV can be sent back to the grid when the EV has excess energy not in used. The simulation result shows the bidirectional operation and the design parameters are maintained. The Total Harmonics Distortion is 1.92% and it is under the IEEE standard of 5% for below 65 kV system. This can make the grid more reliable as large number of batteries can be connected to the grid.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Recognition using Transfer Learning and Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: There is a rapid increase in popularity of the self-driving automobiles. Road safety while keeping the navigation systems efficient necessitates an efficient traffic sign recognition (TSR) system. Exiting methods are computationally complex. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging the adaptability of the transfer learning (TL) models. A pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) is used with transfer learning to improve the system performance. The model is trained on the German traffic sign recognition benchmark (GTSRB) dataset. The proposed work aims to recognize a wider range of traffic signs while keeping computational costs low. The comparison analysis with existing and standard models validates the effectiveness of the proposed model. The suggested approach may significantly increase the recognition capabilities prompting a safer transportation system.

articleTitle: Innovative Glove Design for Enhanced Robotic Hand Control using PWM Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The demand for robotic systems to assist individuals and undertake complex tasks has grown, particularly in enhancing mobility for those with physical disabilities and ensuring safety in hazardous environments. Traditional sensors in robotic hand control systems are often costly, fixed, and lack adaptability. This research presents an innovative glove design integrating rotary potentiometers and three advanced Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) techniques for controlling robotic hands. The glove's increased rotational range, up to 150°, offers enhanced precision and control, making it suitable for diverse applications. We explore the efficacy of Arduino MEGA2650, 555 timers, and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) in generating PWM signals. The Arduino provides flexibility, 555 timers offer cost-effective precision, and ANNs enable adaptive control in complex environments. The study demonstrates that rotary potentiometers offer a reliable and cost-effective alternative to flex sensors, with consistent performance across multiple uses. Furthermore, integrating deep learning models trained on Electromyography (EMG) signals can significantly improve the accuracy and reliability of robotic hand control systems, especially in prosthetic applications. The findings suggest that the proposed system not only broadens the applications of robotic hands but also enhances their functionality and user-friendliness.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Integration topologies with NaS Battery for Hybrid Renewable Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: With ambitious plans for improving renewable penetration in the country, energy storage has become an indispensable solution for integrating it into the Indian grid today. It is crucial that storage is planned and installed in sync with the renewable power systems to avoid integration and grid instability issues in the future. This study was undertaken with the motive of exploring the feasibility of implementing storage solutions for wind-PV hybrid renewable system with the aim of making the system more reliable for scheduling and dispatching. A sizing methodology was proposed using optimization algorithm to evaluate the most optimum capacity required by including battery aging and sizing standards. The sizing methodology of batteries are tested and validated with the data from a hybrid wind-PV system. This paper presents the development and implementation of different energy management strategies and analyzes them to help understand their effects on the performance of the storage system and the HRES. Thus, proved that, battery storage is a feasible and profitable venture for the wind-PV system considered in the study.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling and Analysis of Single and Three-phase Synchronous Buck Converter for EV Battery Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: A comprehensive mathematical model and simulation-based analysis of single and three-phase interleaved synchronous buck converters specifically designed for electric vehicle (EV) battery charging applications is presented in this study. The analysis considers significant parasitic elements of the converter to accurately validate system behavior and performance in practical scenarios. The converter is modeled using the state-space technique to obtain the desired transfer functions, and frequency domain analysis is carried out using Bode plots to validate system stability. A cascaded dual-loop control strategy is implemented to regulate the output voltage. A MATLAB/Simulink model of the system is developed to validate transient and steady-state responses. Comparative simulation analysis is performed to assess key performance metrics, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed compensation technique in both single and three-phase buck converters in EV battery chargers.

articleTitle: Energy Performance Index analysis for optimization of Zero Energy Building performance through PuLP optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)

authors.preferredName: R K D Satya Prasad Gollakota

abstract: The scarcity of fossil fuels and the growing demand for energy-efficient technologies with sustainable approaches have sparked interest among you, the researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders. Your crucial involvement in exploring modern solutions is what's leading to the increasing popularity of energy-efficient buildings, green buildings, and zero-energy buildings as means to achieve energy self-sufficiency. With the growing interest in energy-autonomous buildings, the Energy Performance Index (EPI) emerges as a crucial tool for assessing the performance of Zero-Energy Buildings (ZEBs) or sustainable buildings. This knowledge is essential for accurately evaluating the real performance of ZEBs and their technical validation. This paper proposes a novel approach to applying the PuLP linear programming for low-cost ZEBs by integrating on-site renewable energy sources. The plan begins with integrating heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, passive energy technologies, energy-efficient appliances, and operational protocols to reduce the Energy Performance Index (EPI) and incorporate on-site renewable energy sources. The findings from this research paper, which explores cost-effective alternatives for zero-energy buildings, are promising and can potentially revolutionize the field of sustainable energy technologies, sparking excitement and optimism.

articleTitle: Advanced Strategies for Chattering Reduction in Sliding Mode-Controlled Bidirectional Cuk Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Sliding Mode Control (SMC) is a robust control technique widely used for managing nonlinear systems with uncertainties and disturbances. It has many advantages like Robustness to System Uncertainties, Simple Implementation, Finite-Time Convergence, Insensitivity to Nonlinearities, Stability and Robust Performance. Despite its advantages significant challenge in SMC is the phenomenon of chattering, characterized by high-frequency oscillations of the control signal around the desired sliding surface. This paper provides a comprehensive investigation into the chattering issues associated with HOSMC and ASMC in power converters, examining the causes, consequences, potential mitigation techniques. Comparative analysis explains that, both HOSMC and ASMC improve the dynamic response and stability of bidirectional converters, ensuring efficient and reliable operation.

articleTitle: Agricultural Pest and Disease Detection System using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Crop diseases pose a significant threat to agricultural productivity in Manipur, a state renowned for its rich agricultural heritage and diverse crop cultivation practices. Early detection of these diseases is crucial for safeguarding the region's agricultural sustainability and ensuring food security. In this paper, we present a comprehensive machine learning-based system utilizing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and the U-NET model for detecting crop diseases specifically tailored to the unique agricultural landscape of Manipur, India. Leveraging advanced techniques such as transfer learning with deep learning pre-trained models, including VGG16 and VGG19, we developed a robust system capable of accurately identifying diseased crops, including locally grown vegetables like "Kobiphun" (cabbage), "Kobilei" (cauliflower), "Aloo" (potato), "Khamen Asinba" (tomato), and "Chak-hao" (black rice). The datasets used in this project are purely self-collected primary data, reflecting extensive effort and dedication in gathering high-quality images for training and model development. Our methodology involves detailed image processing, feature extraction demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach in addressing the specific challenges posed by crop diseases in Manipur's agricultural system. The findings highlight the model's high accuracy (over 92%), precision (exceeding 90%), and recall (approaching 100%), indicating its reliability in real-world applications. Additionally, the system's scalability allows for integration with real-time monitoring tools, enhancing its applicability for local farmers. This research contributes to improved disease management practices, enhances the resilience of Manipur's agriculture sector, and ensures the livelihoods of its farming communities.

articleTitle: Enhanced Primary Side Control Strategy in Dynamic Wireless Charging Systems for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) is pivotal in the global effort to reduce carbon emissions and mitigate climate change. As the automotive industry shifts towards zero-emission solutions, the infrastructure for efficient and convenient EV charging becomes increasingly critical. Traditional stationary charging methods present limitations, particularly in terms of convenience and charging efficiency. Dynamic Wireless Charging (DWC) systems emerge as a revolutionary approach, offering continuous power transfer to moving EVs, thereby extending driving ranges and reducing downtime. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of the control strategies employed, their implementation, and their impact on the overall system performance. There is a critical need for data-driven approaches to enhance the flexibility and effectiveness of primary side control mechanisms in DWC systems. The results highlight the potential of dynamic wireless charging technology to implement the EV charging landscape.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode MPPT Control for Grid-Tied Micro Inverters in Dynamic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In recent years, microinverters have become essential components in grid-connected applications, particularly for solar photovoltaic (PV) integration. This study investigates the implementation of Sliding Mode Control (SMC), a robust and reliable control method, for converter regulation based on PV system characteristics. Specifically, this research utilizes a DC-DC converter featuring an impedance source and decoupled control architecture. The proposed control approach minimizes ripple across the DC-link capacitor and enhances grid-side power quality. Both simulation and experimental analyses validate the efficacy of the adaptive sliding mode-like control strategy, demonstrating a superior dynamic response through rapid adaptation to fluctuating environmental conditions, thereby maximizing energy extraction from the PV array. Furthermore, the decoupled control design enables precise, independent regulation of the AC and DC components, resulting in improved power quality and reduced voltage ripple within the microgrid environment.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Tomato Leaf Disease Detection using VGG, Resnet and Mobilenet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The main goal of this study is to differentiate tomato leaves that have been harmed by certain diseases and those have not. The manual interpretation of these leaf diseases requires a lot of work and time. Many models have been created in the past to recognize various plant diseases. Deep learning and computer vision have advanced into potent agricultural technologies in recent years. A comparative analysis of tomato leaf disease detection have been conducted in this paper. The performance of the Resnet152, Resnet50, Mobilenet, MobilenetV2, VGG 19, and VGG 16 networks is compared in terms of F1_Score, Accuracy, Specificity, and Recall. The investigation concludes that the MobilenetV2 network performs better with a maximum accuracy of 97%, recall of 92%, specificity of 99%, F1 score of 95% and the miss-classification of 0.03. Therefore, this method is well suitable for tomato leaf disease detection.

articleTitle: Garbage In, Insights Out: Deep Transfer Learning for Automatic Solid Waste Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Solid waste segregation is a significant global issue. Unlike advanced countries, where the solid waste segregation process is quite streamlined, this is not the case for developing countries, especially in those with large populations. India falls into the latter category and generates about 62 million tons of municipal solid waste annually, of which only about 20% is treated. This paper provides a comparative study of four competitive convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures (viz. ResNet50, EfficientNet, InceptionNet, and VGG16) to derive insights from waste-related data and classify them accurately into appropriate categories. These four CNN architectures were trained using a custom-made dataset consisting of 5392 images from 24 classes, covering the most commonly occurring categories of solid waste. The experimental results suggest that the proposed system can automatically segregate waste into appropriate categories, which can help develop a proper waste management system.

articleTitle: A Multi-Level Hybrid Classifier and Ensemble Feature Selection Based Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: As the Internet and related technologies have advanced rapidly, so have the opportunities for infiltration and the number of hidden dangers to network security. Hence, in order to prevent attacks on networks, it is essential to improve intrusion detection systems' ability to identify and stop them. Consequently, researchers have come up with a number of ways to use network monitoring data to find network intrusions quickly and accurately. This has led to the use of network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). In this paper, a signature-based intrusion detection system (SIDS) using a multi-level hybrid system is introduced in order to detect and classify attack types. Experiments conducted on the UNSW-NB15 dataset indicate that the system under consideration has a detection capability of 99.87% for binary attacks and 93.68% for multiclass attacks. The results of the experiments show that the suggested multi-level hybrid approach can effectively find network intrusions and perform better than current intrusion detection systems (IDS).

articleTitle: Electrical conductivity based oil detection and skimming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Oil spills are a serious threat to marine life and often result from industrial activities. To combat the problem of floating oil, oil skimming is a crucial technique that uses polyurethane (PU) belts to adsorb oil effluents. However, a fresh method has been created that involves incorporating electric conductivity properties into oil skimmers. This creative approach makes use of the different conductivity properties of water and oil, allowing for the detection of oil on water. As oil is bad conductor of electricity and water is good conductor, by sensing the current flow we can get to know the presence of oil, because it does not allow current to flow. The prototype for this project is propelled by a BLDC motor and controlled through Bluetooth from a pre-built app, using the HC-05 Bluetooth module. An Arduino UNO R3 microcontroller monitors the output of the voltage sensor and relays this information to the operator. With the potential to greatly improve oil skimming operations and minimize the environmental impact of oil spills, this innovation will be a promising development.

articleTitle: SEZE Converter Based V2G and G2V Technologies in a Microgrid using PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This study proposes the integration framework of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and grid-to-vehicle (G2V) technologies within a microgrid utilizing modular converters for DC energy transfer. V2G and G2V systems facilitate the interaction of electric vehicles (EVs) with the grid, enabling them to both import and export electricity. This research introduces a fast-charging setup employing SEPIC (Single-Ended Primary Inductor Converter) and ZETA converters combined together to form a SEZE converter. The design comprises of individual components of EV batteries coupled to the core component of charger which features a bidirectional DC-DC converter. Simulation results indicate that the control system exhibits minimal harmonic distortion in grid current and demonstrates excellent dynamic performance regarding DC bus voltage and charging station stability. Overall, this paper employs a fast-charging configuration to demonstrate V2G-G2V technology in a microgrid using a PI controller.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Distance Protection in UPFC-Compensated Transmission Networks with Integrated Converter-Interfaced Renewable Energy Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Today, the Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) stands out as one of the most versatile FACTS devices, extensively deployed on transmission lines. However, the presence of UPFC device in the transmission line affects voltage and current signals at the relay location. The commonly used distance relays face greater protection challenges when such compensated transmission networks are integrated with solar plants. This paper evaluates the distance relay performance in five-bus test system by simulating a double phase to ground fault at seventy percent length of the UPFC-compensated transmission line from the relay bus, with and without solar power plant. The quadrilateral relay characteristics are adjusted to ensure fault detection up to a resistance of 10 Ω with synchronous generator. However, when the synchronous generator is replaced with a solar plant, the relay begins to malfunction with fault resistances as low as 0.5 Ω under these operating conditions. To prevent relay maloperation, the tripping boundaries are adjusted. The apparent impedance measured by the relay falls within this modified characteristics, thus enabling accurate fault detection.

articleTitle: Vibration Analysis of Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Switched Reluctance Motors (SRM) continue to draw consideration in the industry because of their magnet-free design, natural ability to tolerate faults, and ease of assembly. Nevertheless, SRM exhibits vibration and torque ripple as disadvantages compared to other electric motors. The vibration can be reduced by employing appropriate geometry and control approaches. Vibration analysis plays a crucial role in determining the proper motor type. This study examines the vibration analysis of an 8/6 SRM designed for Electric Vehicle (EV) applications. The radial force was obtained from an electromagnetic Finite Element Analysis (FEA) study. This analysis is conducted using Ansys MOTORCAD, an electromagnetic design tool. Following an analytical determination, the natural frequencies are contrasted with the outcomes of the simulation. An NVH analysis is carried out to ensure that the excitation frequencies do not match the natural frequencies.

articleTitle: Modeling Enablers for the Blockchain Technology Adoption for Sustainable Logistics Practices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Blockchain technology may be a vital tool in paving the way to sustainable practices in logistics activities. This article evaluates the Enablers of Block Chain Technology Adoption (EBTA) in Sustainable Logistics Activities (SLA). Sustainable logistics reduces environmental degradation by reducing carbon and other resource consumption to emissions while providing lasting supply chain efficiencies and cost savings, making this practice in economies very liable for responsible economic growth and corporate social responsibility. Based on a thorough literature review, seventeen key enablers are identified. The top five EBTA are identified through the experts' opinions on the importance of enablers in the Logistics sector. The Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) method is applied to uncover their cause-and-effect relationships. The major drivers identified are Decentralization and Traceability, and the remaining EBTA explains the dependency.

articleTitle: Optimizing Power Quality varify on UPQC and Soft Computing Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: One of the most critical challenges in today’s rapidly expanding electrical world is maintaining power quality, efficiently distributing electricity without significant losses is difficult, and it's crucial to ensure that the quality of power remains within acceptable limits.
