The versatile dual control methodology of the Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) offers an effective solution to manage power distribution and address power quality issues. UPQC compensates for both current and voltage irregularities in reactive loads while also eliminating harmonics in the load current under distorted supply conditions. This project explores various techniques to enhance power efficiency, starting with the use of a UPQC integrated with a PID controller to address power efficiency challenges. To further improve power quality, an advanced solution using a UPQC with an ANFIS controller has been implemented, significantly enhancing performance.

articleTitle: Power Quality Analysis in Microgrid Using Unified Power Quality Conditioner and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Power quality challenges have emerged as a significant concern in the implementation of smart grid systems. Active power filters (APFs) are commonly employed to tackle these issues due to their rapid filtering capabilities and ability to provide instantaneous compensation. To address problems related to voltage irregularities and load current disturbances, the Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) has been introduced within microgrid environments. Maintaining precise control over the DC link capacitor voltage is essential to ensure the UPQC delivers optimal performance. Typically, a PI controller is utilized to maintain and regulate the voltage across the DC link capacitor. The various methods for determining PI control parameters are Ziegler-Nichols Method, Pole Placement Method, Frequency Response Methods, Optimization Techniques, State-Space Methods etc. This study presents the integration of a UPQC equipped with a Particle Swarm Optimization-based PI controller alongside renewable energy sources such as wind and solar photovoltaic systems to improve power quality. A microgrid simulation model incorporating the UPQC is developed using MATLAB 2022A, and the results are thoroughly analyzed and discussed. "

articleTitle: Closed Loop operation of Transformer-less Inverter in Voltage and Current Control mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: A single stage single phase inverter topology derived from Cuk converter, with an input switched inductor, suitable for Photovoltaic-Grid interface is implemented in voltage control and current control mode. Voltage and current control strategies, controller tuning with d-q transformation for active power injection to grid and how it was validated by simulation are detailed in the paper. Simulation results are presented for a power level of 250W, then tracking the voltage/current reference was observed in standalone and grid connected mode of operation individually. The proportional and integral constants of the current controller is calculated based on the value of the output filter inductor and External Series Resistance (ESR) of the output filter capacitor. These calculated values gave good results as presented. Additionally, total harmonic distortion was measured to be less than 2% for a voltage gain of 3.42.

articleTitle: Assessment of Li-Ion Battery Performance for Electric Vehicles using Different Drive Cycles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Electric vehicles have become a critical requirement of the future to help in reducing carbon emission. Nevertheless, numerous limitations exist associated with the extensive adoption of electric vehicles. One of the main limitations is the proper choice and sizing of battery packs for the electric vehicle. The typical cost of battery for an electric vehicle accounts for about 40% of the total cost of the vehicle. This paper is primarily focused on Li-ion battery modeling and simulation studies of a 2RC model of a Liion cell using difference drive cycle. This work also describes the development and sizing i.e. parameters calculation of a lithium-ion battery pack for use in electric vehicle applications. The modelling of an electric vehicle based on the battery is considered and simulated in MATLAB Simulink where different graphs and characteristics for the electric vehicle using the calculated battery parameters are obtained. The purpose of consideration of this battery model is to investigate the battery capability and their behaviour across the different drive cycles. Finally, the assessment of Li-ion battery is reported in this work by considering various drive cycles. It is also observed that the FTP-75 is more suited for practical implementation among all the considered drive cycles.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Permanent Magnet and Permanent Magnet Less Special Machines using Electromagnetic Analysis for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Electrical vehicles (EVs) have emerged as the most indispensable medium of transport globally due to their low running, and maintenance cost, lowest carbon footprint, tax benefits, high energy efficiency, and very convenient to charge at home. Permanent Magnet (PM) and PM Less electric motors are used extensively in E-Vehicles because of high power and torque density, lower rotor inertia, and higher efficiency. Therefore, this paper analyzed four different EV motors such as interior permanent synchronous motor (IPMSM), PM brushless DC motor (PMBLDC), PM less switched reluctance motor (PMSRM) and universal motor. The investigation of speed-torque, efficiency, power and performance characteristics is analyzed for all four motors. These performance characteristics are analysed using Finite Element Analysis in the ANSYS MAXWELL simulation software. The results are compared and humble attempts have been made to ensure the most optimum and economical special machine for EV applications.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study of Various Advanced Control Techniques for PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are crucial in modern applications due to their high torque-to- weight ratio, efficiency, and precise speed control. They are widely used in robotics, electric vehicles, and renewable energy systems. In commercial settings where accuracy is important, closed-loop control systems are preferred over simpler voltage-to-frequency (V/f) open-loop controls. This work examines various control methods for PMSMs, focusing on the commonly used proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller and more advanced techniques like direct torque control (DTC), maximum torque per ampere (MTPA), and model predictive control (MPC). The PID controller remains popular in industrial environments due to its simplicity and effective error correction. However, advanced methods like model predictive control (MPC) provide better torque control and energy efficiency, especially in variable load conditions. This study compares the PID approach with the more advanced technique MPC model, highlighting their advantages in improving the performance of PMSMs for industrial and commercial use.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Different Optimization Techniques for SoC Estimation in EV Battery Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Battery management system (BMS) is an embedded system in electric vehicles (EVs) that is responsible for maintaining the performance and efficiency of a battery which allows proper charging and discharging by estimating state-of-charge (SoC), balancing cell voltages, etc. This article compares how well two machine learning (ML) models: specifically, long short-term memory (LSTM) and recurrent neural networks (RNN) estimate the SoC of EV batteries. The performance of each model is assessed by their mean squared error (MSE) values, which are the main evaluation metrics. Preliminary results indicate that the LSTM model, which has more sophisticated handling of long-stage dependencies, classifies the better SoCs than other method like RNN. These results represent an important contribution to the selection of optimal optimization techniques used in battery management, and provide a basis for further research and development. Within the Python programming environment, the models are generated and tested using data from the "Panasonic 18650PF" battery.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Load Forecasting using Efficient Feature Extraction Scheme in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The smart grid requires the integration of emerging technologies for the digitalization of the demand side. This study deals with short-term load forecasting using candidate machine learning models to utilize demand-side technologies. The dataset of Panama’s national grid has been implemented with new features through correlation mapping and tested for the five machine-learning models. The results illustrate that Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boost (XGBoost), two ensemble-based machine learning models, perform better considering evaluation metrics, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). After that, machine learning models are also tested with sequential historical data and used as extracted features for hourly and weekly prediction. It shows that model performances have improved if more sequential historical data is used. The study’s findings will be beneficial in using these outperformed models to anticipate an accurate load for current intelligent energy transitions.

articleTitle: Study of Grounding System Transients in Two-Layer Soil Structure during Lightning Events
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This article explores the response of earthing electrodes embedded in two-layer soils when exposed to lightning, focusing on factors like soil ionization, resistivity, and permittivity. The research investigates the performance of vertical rods, horizontal conductors, and grounding grids within two-layer soil structure. Transmission line modeling (TLM) is employed, incorporating the nonlinear conductance phenomenon to model grounding systems effectively. The developed model takes into account frequency-dependent soil parameters to study the transient behavior of these systems. Soil ionization is modeled by considering nonlinear conductance as a time-dependent function, along with the presence of residual resistivity. The grounding models are tested against lightning current impulses of varying magnitudes and rise times to assess GPR, transient behavior, and grounding impulse impedance. To enhance the accuracy of the study, both apparent and effective diameters of the grounding electrodes are considered. The results obtained from the model are validated by comparing them with other developed model that showing good agreement. The impulse impedances of vertically and horizontally buried grounding electrodes in two layer soil structure with different electrical characteristics under a 5 kA peak impulse are evaluated. Peak voltages at the current injection point are also calculated for horizontal electrodes, considering variations in length and soil electrical properties

articleTitle: Optimising Breast Cancer Identification and Categorisation by Hyperparameter Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Breast cancer is curable if caught early enough to stop it from spreading. In spite of this, misdiagnosis of breast cancer contributes to its continued status as the world's largest cause of mortality for women. Videos of breast cytology are analysed using deep learning frameworks to enhance early detection and categorisation. Layers based on convolution and pooling are used in these frameworks to extract features, and then dense layers are used for classification. To distinguish between malignant and benign cells, models such as neural networks using convolution and DenseNet undergo training, validation, and testing. In terms of both diagnosis and classification of breast tumours, the suggested approach performs better than CNN (Convolutional neural network) and DenseNet, despite different size of batches and learning rates. By increasing the effectiveness of these models through hyperparameter tuning, histological pictures can be used to make diagnoses that are more accurate.

articleTitle: Optimizing Erythemato-Squamous Disease Diagnosis with Cutting-Edge Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This The goal of this project paper is to create a machine learning-enhanced diagnostic system for Erythemato-Squamous diseases (ESD) that uses the Gradient Booster algorithm, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Logistic Regression (LR) to classify various strains of the disease. of LR, the system used a dataset of clinical, historical, and demographic data to obtain an astounding 98.64% accuracy rate. This demonstrates how the approach may significantly enhance ESD diagnosis and treatment choices. The reliability of the findings was confirmed using an additional dataset, pointing to noteworthy developments in the field of dermatological healthcare and creating new avenues for the application of machine learning in medical diagnostics

articleTitle: A Sliding Mode Control Approach for Maximum Power Point Tracking and Efficiency Optimization of Photovoltaic Systems in Isolated Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In the present scenario, PV systems are in high demand due to directly converting solar energy into electric power, generating power without damaging the environment. The sophisticated topology consists of a Boost Converter that raises the PV voltage to a level where the inverter can produce the necessary single-phase AC output voltage of 230V, 50Hz. A single-phase inverter is employed to sequentially process the output of the step-up converter sequentially, ensuring the generation of the requisite amount and frequency of electric energy. To optimize power extraction from the PV system, the perturb and observe MPPT algorithm is utilized. This study focuses on constructing an SMC tailored to the specific type of PV cell and its characteristics to achieve the desired inverter output voltage. The design of the Sliding Mode Controller and system stability analysis using a state space model are the primary goals of the work. Efficient tracking is used to confirm the controller's performance and achieve the intended 230V output voltage response. The properties of frequency response are used to derive stability studies. The dynamic and nonlinear characteristics of the load are analyzed and juxtaposed with traditional Proportional Integral (PI) and Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controllers. The Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the output voltage adheres to IEEE 519 standards, while the frequency remains in compliance with IEEE 1547.1 standards. The suggested topology be made for stand-alone applications using MATLAB/SIMULINK, and OPAL-RT is used for validation.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Energy storage system for an hybrid PV-Wind Powered Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Owing to their emission-free nature and sustainability, hybrid renewable energy sources (RESs) have emerged as a formidable alternative to traditional energy production facilities. Nevertheless, two unfavorable aspects that exacerbate the issue of system suitable scaling are the cost of energy (COE) and the intermittent nature of RESs. The goal of this study is to size hybrid grid-connected photovoltaic-wind power systems as efficiently as possible using real-time hourly data on solar and wind irradiation, as well as the amount of energy required at a given site. The suggested technique may match the local demand for energy supply with the system's least life cycle cost by determining the optimal size. In order to provide accurate estimates of life cycle costs and benefits, the actual hourly electricity retail and market prices were used in the case study used to evaluate the approach in this article. The battery-powered HRES system was examined for various battery capacity combinations, simulated using a range of energy management techniques, and its operation was assessed in comparison to planned power dispatches. With the HRES providing power with enhanced dependability and combining peak shaving and ramp rate limiting characteristics with the stored energy, the findings shown that battery storage systems are a highly viable and lucrative endeavor.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Auto Insurance Fraud detection: Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Insurance fraud is a massive burden for the industry and causes billions in economic damage yearly. This research deals with the difficulties in fraud detection of insurance companies, focusing on machine learning approaches. Based on factual data from an insurance company the study kind use SVM, Decision Tree model, Random Forest Ada Boost Gradient Boosting and Stochastic Gradient Boosting, XGBoosts Extra Trees in this case. The assessment of this models is through various proper analysis which include confusion matrix and main performance metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and so on. This study aims to provide insights that would be beneficial to improve the fraud detection strategy in insurance industry by comparing the performance of models used.

articleTitle: A Review survey on MCDM Technique for usage in Site Selection of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This review explores the application of Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) techniques in selecting optimal sites for renewable energy power plants. By examining 85 papers from Science Direct published between 2010 and 2023, the study outlines five key stages of the site selection process: criterion selection, data normalization, criteria weighting, alternative evaluation, and outcome validation. The analysis reveals varying criteria for different renewable energy sources like solar, wind, and tidal energy. Popular methods like the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and geographic information systems (GIS) are frequently employed in criteria selection and alternative assessment. The study identifies best practices and challenges across different energy sources, highlighting the role of MCDM in achieving sustainable and efficient site selection for renewable energy projects.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase Symmetrical Multilevel Inverter fed Induction Motor Pump system for Irrigation Applications : Symmetrical MLI for Irrigation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: A thorough analysis of modulation techniques for a Multilevel Inverter-fed Induction Motor water pumping system is crucial for optimizing performance and reliability. In this study, key factors such as harmonic content of output power, switching frequency, and system complexity are carefully evaluated to determine the most suitable modulation technique. The existing literature highlights various approaches to reducing harmonic distortion and enhancing inverter performance, which informed the selection process in this work.The proposed system architecture effectively minimizes the number of switching devices, circuit losses, voltage stress, mounting space, and overall inverter costs, aligning with the advancements presented in earlier studies on inverter efficiency and cost-reduction strategies. The Phase Disposition Level Shift (PDLS) method is employed to generate triggering impulses for the switching devices, a widely recognized approach in recent research for achieving balanced voltage levels and improved control.Furthermore, the pump design is tailored for irrigation land spanning 50 acres, offering a practical application of the system. The experimental setup validates the inverter's operational performance, and the results corroborate the findings from prior research on multilevel inverters in water pumping applications. The outcomes of this study reinforce the potential of the proposed system to enhance efficiency while addressing the challenges identified in the literature.

articleTitle: Loss Reduction and Power Quality Enhancement of Distribution system Using FACTS Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The Study emphasizes the crucial role of D-STATCOM placement and sizing in enhancing network efficiency and reliability. Leveraging PSO offers a systematic and efficient approach for optimizing D-FACTS devices, contributing to more resilient and sustainable energy infrastructures. The given results highlights the practical feasibility of PSO-based optimization techniques in real-world distribution network management. The approach is implemented on radial distribution network of the IEEE 33-bus, with PSO determining optimal D-STATCOM locations and sizes at buses 3, 6, and 33, with corresponding sizes of 515 KVar, 475 KVar, and 207 KVar respectively. This optimization strategy results in a substantial reduction in total network power losses (21.26%) and significant voltage profile improvement (0.8542%). Furthermore, system reconfiguration is performed, with PSO identifying optimal DSTATCOM locations and sizes at buses 33, 4, and 5, with sizes of 559 KVar, 805 KVar, and 275 KVar respectively. After reconfiguration, PSO achieves a greater reduction in total power losses (26.58%) and remarkable voltage profile enhancement (0.8796%). Notably, the computational efficiency of PSO is commendable.

articleTitle: Solar Power Feed Wireless Power Transfer System to Charge EV Battery Using Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This paper discuss about solar powered wireless power transfer (WPT) for battery charging system using proportional integral (PI) and fuzzy logic controller (FLC). The WPT used in electric vehicle is popular due to the absence of wire connections and unstable operations of converter voltage, current and power can be analyzed and controlled by the system. The proposed methods of conventional PI controller and fuzzy logic controllers are implemented using MATLAB/Simulink and analyzed the output voltage and error parameters. The hardware model is implemented using PIC16F877A microcontroller and the output wave forms are analyzed. The simulation outputs of PI and fuzzy controller settling time are 0.34sec and 0.04sec. the output voltage is 18V. Hardware output is compared with the software output.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Car Parking System with Route Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Smart car parking management system integration is a necessary component of transforming current infrastructure into smart cities. Finding parking spaces becomes more difficult, especially in cities with large population densities, such as metropolitan areas. The issue of finding parking spaces in mall and complex basement parking is due to inadequate spaces and inappropriate parking space use. Thus, this paper aims to offer a solution that uses mobile apps and the Internet of Things (IoT). The goal is to direct people to the unoccupied parking slot with the guided route. This system consists of an LCD, a servo motor, LEDs, a Wi-Fi-enabled ESP32 module, an Arduino ATmega2560, and IR sensors. The Arduino ATmega2560 microcontroller is used to gather and interpret real-time sensor data, and The LEDs are utilized for indoor navigation to identify the location of available parking slots. The ESP32 Wi-Fi module then transmits the parking information data to the Blynk cloud, which can be accessed through the Blynk smartphone app. The system prototype has been put through actual testing to ensure that it is both functional and applicable. The findings illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in monitoring parking space occupancy and delivering real-time data to the Blynk cloud server.

articleTitle: SR motor (6/4) Drive, design and control using MPPT and Cuk converter for EV application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The switching reluctance motor (SRM) is a longstanding member of the Electric Machines family, valued for its straightforward construction, durability, and cost-effective manufacturing, making it well-suited for industrial applications. This paper explores speed control of an SRM using the feedback control method combined with a proportional integral (PI) controller. The design, modelling, and simulation of a 6/4 SRM have been carried out. The proposed technique is readily applicable in implementations utilizing more powerful CPUs. A 60KW, 8000RPM machine prototype was designed, constructed, and tested under load and no-load conditions using single pulse and hysteresis band current regulation. This machine could be used for direct drive in washing machines as well as electric automobiles. The study suggests designing an MPPT controller and Position Sensor for a 6/4 SRM under various load circumstances. The simulation's outcomes were contrasted.

articleTitle: Demand Side Management with NILM in a Prepaid Smart Metering Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: With advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) in place, an important task on the consumer side is to apply residential load pattern recognition to provide the consumer with options to fulfill their energy requirements given various constraints, especially in a pre-payment-based energy metering system. On the utility side, Energy Management involves the planning and coordination of energy production (supply) and energy consumption (demand) to meet certain requirements taking into consideration, environmental and economic constraints. Managing of the consumer side energy is known as Demand Side Management (DSM). With Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) increasingly penetrating the system it is important to balance supply and demand at the consumer end. Monitoring and Control are important facets of demand-side management as they make possible the control loop action (measuring and actuation). Advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning along with the concept of the Internet of Things have led to various advances in Demand Side Management. This paper introduces a framework for DSM using the concepts of Non Intrusive Load Monitoring for prepaid system to fulfill their energy requirements whatever the constraints. Supply and Demand must be met by monitoring and control of the Source based on availability and cost, and the Load based on individual consumption, curtailability and incentives.

articleTitle: Power Generation in Electric Vehicle Through Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Wind turbines are used conventionally for the generation of electric power at different locations at higher altitudes. These conventional wind turbines rely on the atmospheric wind speed to drive it and produce power. Apart from this, another alternative way to produce power through atmospheric wind along with vehicle speed is by installing a wind turbine in the vehicle itself. while traveling Vehicle speed is combined with atmospheric wind speed, and it enhances the wind speed available to the wind turbine. The impact of different wind types available to the wind turbine on power generation is analyzed. Additionally, Range extension by the EVs with different types of wind speeds is analyzed in official hours of traveling time. Furthermore, the analysis of wind energy production in EVs relative to other renewable energy sources is examined during official working hours, along with the challenges encountered by wind energy generation in EVs.

articleTitle: Prediction of Smartphone Prices in the market using Machine Learning Algorithms: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Smartphones and mobile devices have become a fundamental part in our modern world, transforming the way we communicate, work and access information. Their significance lies in providing access to a vast number of applications and services. Primarily, smartphones serve as a powerful communication tool enabling us to contact people across large geographical boundaries. With features such as calls, texts and various messaging apps, individuals can communicate easily. As technology continues to advance, predicting the prices of mobile phones becomes crucial for various stakeholders in the market. This is where Machine Learning (ML) techniques have a key role. Regression and Classification methods are important components of these techniques, each serving a different and distinct purpose. In this study we apply Regression methods such as SVR and LSTM as well as Classification methods such as K-Means, KNN, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting to categorize data in predefined classes. Comparison of each ML technique finally conclude which gives the most accurate prediction. Smartphones and mobiles play a pivotal role in the interconnected world, impacting information access and productivity. Predicting the prices of mobile phones through Machine Learning techniques is essential for making informed decisions in a dynamic market. This study can provide tools necessary to anticipate future trends, benefiting consumers, manufacturers and investors alike.

articleTitle: Investigation of ATH and SiO2 Nanofillers to Improve the Performance Characteristics of Outdoor Porcelain Insulators under Desert Environment Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Porcelain insulators have been widely used in outdoor conditions due to their higher electrical resistance compared to polymers. This work presents an experimental study of different performance characteristics using Alumina Tri Hydrate [ATH] and Silicon Di Oxide [SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>] nanofillers with different ratios and proportions. The nanocomposite solution was synthesized and characterized after incorporation with different concentrations. Porcelain insulators are ideal for locations where there are frequent changes in temperature and also extreme and dry conditions. In this paperwork, flashover and performance tests were conducted on nanocoated insulator samples under artificially created sandstorm desert conditions. The addition of nanofillers improved the breakdown voltage and reduced the percentage of porosity and surface roughness and the lifetime of the insulator samples at an appreciable rate. In this study, the effects of sandstorms, and thermal and electrical performances have been investigated in detail.

articleTitle: Comparative Machine Learning-based Techno-Economic Feasibility Analysis of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This article provides a thorough analysis of the financial and technological impacts of four hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) setup with the goal of supplying Quantanics Techserv Pvt.Ltd, Tamil Nadu, India, with renewable electricity. The investigation emphasizes grid-dependent hybrid energy systems configured optimally to ensure uninterrupted power supply to workplaces. Initially, a techno-economic analysis is conducted using HOMER software to determine the economic feasibility and technical viability of the energy systems. The integrated configuration of solar PV, grid, diesel generator, battery, and converter show the lowest levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) at ₹3.05million per kWh and the lowest overall system performance among all the systems studied, according to the economic analysis ₹4.36 million is the net present cost (NPC). Nevertheless, technical examination reveals that the configuration made up of grid, solar PV, converters, and batteries renders the 29.9% renewable fraction. Following that, five machine learning algorithm like artificial neural network, decision tree, random forest, linear regression and XG-boost assess the different configuration and balance the techno-economic (TE) factors to cross-verify and predict system performance based on evaluation metrics to achieve sustainable and efficient energy usage. This research contributes to the growing field of sustainable energy solutions by integrating advanced modelling and predictive tools. The study's findings reveal that the ANN regression model outperforms other models, showcasing lower root mean square error and higher R2 values in techno-economic assessments of the commercial buildings considered. These results render valuable insights in to the setup and optimal system of HRES for on-grid applications in urban commercial building, considering their technical and economic aspects.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of PI and Fuzzy Logic Controllers for Speed Control of Permanent Magnet Sensorless Brushless DC Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: PMBLDC Motors are a commercial example due to the strong power generated by the three-phase semiconductor bridge. This paper underscores the critical role of rotor position sensors in ensuring accurate commutation, facilitating the sequential activation of power devices for optimal motor operation. Conventionally, speed control in PMBLDC motors relies on proportional-integral (PI) controllers, which, while effective under ideal conditions, struggle with nonlinearities, disturbances, and parameter variations due to their reliance on linear models. To address these challenges, this research proposes a FLC for BLDC speed regulation. Leveraging its inherent ability to handle nonlinearities and uncertainties, the FLC offers improved dynamic response, robustness against disturbances, and adaptability to varying operating conditions compared to PI controllers. Drawing parallels from conventional Proportional-Integral Controllers (PIC), the FLC design enhances speed response quality, optimizing motor performance. MATLAB simulations are conducted to evaluate and compare the performance of PMBLDC drives under PI and Fuzzy Logic control schemes, demonstrating the FLC's efficacy in achieving superior speed control and stability across a wide range of operating scenarios. This study contributes valuable insights into advancing motor control technologies, particularly in enhancing the efficiency and reliability of PMBLDC motors in industrial applications.

articleTitle: A Unified Design Method for FOPID Controllers in Active Suspension Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This study explored the use of fractional order PID (FOPID) controllers for active vehicle suspension, addressing the challenges of discretization for real-time application. Simulations on a quarter-car model were conducted to compare the performance of a novel direct delta domain FOPID (delta-FOPID) with traditional z-domain FOPID and continuous time FOPID implementations. The results indicated that the delta-FOPID outperformed the other methods, especially at very low sampling times, where the z-domain FOPID showed numerical instability. The delta-FOPID’s improved accuracy and stability, achieved by closely approximating continuous time control behavior as the sampling time (delta) approaches zero, led to significant enhancements in ride comfort, road handling, and suspension deflection. These findings underscore the potential of fractional order control and direct delta domain discretization for creating advanced and robust active suspension systems.

articleTitle: Efficient Modeling of Synchronous Machines for Transient Simulation of Marine Electrical Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Synchronous machines are employed in various applications, including marine electric power and propulsion systems. This paper proposes a multirate constant-parameter voltage-behind-reactance (CP-VBR) synchronous machine model to improve the efficiency of electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations of multi-machine marine electrical systems. The proposed multirate modeling technique considers the difference in transient behaviors between the stator (fast) subsystem and the rotor and mechanical (slow) subsystems. Allowing larger time steps for the slow subsystem enhances the overall computational efficiency. The proposed multirate synchronous machine model is implemented using the custom-defined library in PSCAD/EMTDC and demonstrated in transient studies of marine electrical systems. It is shown that by increasing the slow subsystem time step by a factor of five with respect to the fast subsystem, appreciable computational gains may be achieved while maintaining good numerical accuracy.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Government Policies on Phasing Out Single-Use Plastics: An Industry-Level Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The rising concern over the environmental impact of single-use plastics has led governments worldwide to implement stricter measures aimed at reducing their usage. This study seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of these government policies by assessing the response of various industries and the corresponding changes in plastic pollution over time. The primary objective is to offer actionable recommendations for policymakers and industry leaders to enhance the effectiveness of existing regulations and improve compliance management systems. Through an industry-level analysis, this paper leverages a comprehensive dataset on global plastic pollution and production data across key sectors to measure the impact of policy interventions in reducing plastic waste. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is employed to model the dynamics of policy enforcement, industry adaptation mechanisms, and the lagged responses observed across different industries. The results reveal significant disparities in how industries respond to new regulations—some adopt innovative practices, while others struggle with compliance. The study provides valuable insights for policymakers seeking to refine regulations and for industries aiming to align with sustainability goals. Ultimately, the research contributes to the literature on sustainable development by examining the interplay between environmental policies and industry practices.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based Automated Tooth and Anomaly Classification in OPG X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Recent advancements in computer science and machine learning have revolutionised the landscape of Medical Science, particularly in leveraging algorithms to support healthcare professionals. This study introduces a novel method for automatically detecting and classifying teeth and anomalies from Orthopantomogram (OPG) X-ray images utilising transfer learning techniques. Our approach focused on distinguishing between two types of teeth (incisors and molars) and identifying two anomalies (cap and impacted teeth). By harnessing the capabilities of pre-trained deep learning models, specifically VGG16 and InceptionV3, we developed specialised models tailored to this task. Through fine-tuning a dedicated dataset of OPG X-ray images, we achieved classification accuracies of 98% and 99% for VGG16 and InceptionV3, respectively. These findings underscore the potential of these models to significantly enhance dental diagnostics by offering precise and efficient automated tooth classification. Such advancements promise to streamline diagnostic workflows, mitigate human error, and ultimately improve accessibility to reliable dental care solutions. Future research will expand this work by enlarging the dataset and exploring advanced architectures to further enhance the classification accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Analysis of Charging and Discharging Characteristics Across Various Battery Types
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The charging and discharging behaviours of lead-acid and lithium-ion batteries, individually and in combination, differ. Lead-acid batteries are valued for their affordability and quick discharge, while lithium-ion batteries are preferred for their lighter weight, faster charging, and better thermal management. Integrating these batteries, especially in automotive applications, introduces challenges in efficiently managing their charging and discharging processes. This paper identifies key inefficiencies through experimental analysis and proposes a method to determine battery energy capacity accurately, considering operational and environmental factors. The findings aim to improve the reliability and efficiency of systems using mixed battery types.

articleTitle: Implementation of models for Demand forecasting for e-commerce using time series forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The study delves into the significance of demand forecasting within the e-commerce realm, crucial for businesses to anticipate future customer needs and optimize inventory management and resource allocation strategies. Focusing on employing time series forecasting methodologies, specifically XGBOOST and SARIMAX (Seasonal AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average with eXogenous factors) models, the research aims to predict demand accurately in e-commerce scenarios. By analyzing historical sales data and integrating pertinent external variables like promotional events and seasonal trends, these models endeavor to forecast forthcoming demand trends for a variety of products or services offered by e-commerce platforms. The investigation scrutinizes the intricacies of XGBOOST and SARIMAX models, highlighting their merits and limitations in the context of e-commerce demand forecasting. Moreover, the study assesses model performance using metrics like Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) to gauge accuracy and reliability in demand prediction. The insights gleaned from this study contribute to advancing demand forecasting techniques in e-commerce, offering valuable guidance for businesses aiming to refine operational efficiency and elevate customer satisfaction through precise demand projections. The SARIMA model deployed in this work has a MAPE value of 0.027 which is better than any previously formed SARIMA models on this particular dataset. The XGBOOST model implemented in this work has RMSE value of 2852.098 which is lesser than any of the work done on this dataset before. Also the calculated accuracy comes out to be 98.348% for XGBOOST which is remarkable and is best on this data.

articleTitle: Detection of Apple Plant Diseases using Leaf Images through Convolution Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Effective identification and classification of plant diseases are critical for maintaining agricultural productivity and ensuring food security. With recent advancements in computer vision, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have emerged as powerful tools for diagnosing crop diseases. This research presents a novel approach for detecting apple plant diseases through the analysis of leaf images using CNNs. We utilize the PlantVillage dataset, which comprises a diverse collection of healthy and diseased apple leaf images. The dataset undergoes rigorous preprocessing to enhance image quality, followed by training and evaluation of the CNN models. Our approach achieves remarkable results, demonstrating an accuracy of 99.67%, precision of 98.23%, and F1 score of 99.04%. These findings affirm the robustness of our CNN-based model in accurately classifying various apple diseases. This research not only provides a reliable method for early disease detection but also emphasizes its significance in optimizing crop yield and safeguarding food security. By facilitating timely interventions, our proposed framework has the potential to mitigate the impact of diseases in apple orchards and can be extended to broader applications in precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Developing Game AI for Classic Games Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: New accomplishments have contributed widely to game development especially with respect to production of intelligent game playing entities. Most of the archetypal approaches for designing AI in games fail to work properly in complex and real-time environments with huge action space. This research addresses these challenges by utilizing reinforcement learning (RL) techniques to design AI models for two well-known games: Snake and Mario. The main challenge in the Snake game is to find the best action within a given state in a discrete state-action space. To solve this, we apply Q-learning, an uncomplicated, but highly effective RL algorithm that aims to accumulate the maximum reward by learning from previous experiences. The reason for Mario being more challenging than the other one is that Mario has a high dimensional input space and a continuous action space. For this, we use Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), one of the most effective methods of reinforcement learning applicable in environments with the continuous decision space and stochastic nonlinear differential equations. This paper describes the design, deployment, and evaluation of these Reinforcement Learning agents where the major difficulties and the rectified methodologies are described. This study compares the efficiency of the application of Q-learning and PPO and shows how these approaches are more effective than the classical AI technologies in the context of gaming environments and bring valuable contributions toward further enhancement of game AI.

articleTitle: Registration Plate Recognition Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Security, law enforcement, and traffic management all depend on effective vehicle registration plate detection. Accuracy and speed are hampered by the real-world complexity that current systems frequently struggle with, such as varied lighting conditions and camera angles. Delays in law enforcement, traffic jams, and security flaws can all result from inaccurate or sluggish detection. Our approach makes use of the EfficientDet model, which is renowned for its great speed and precision. We carefully fine-tune the model and use focus loss to mitigate class imbalance. An increasingly safe and effective world is made possible by this flexible technology, which improves traffic control, security, and law enforcement. Our goal is to simplify vehicle identification and enhance overall road safety and security by tackling the difficulties presented by real-world situations.

articleTitle: Raspberry Pi Controlled Automated Residential System with Integrated Alexa Voice Service
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In recent years, home automation has witnessed significant advancements, with voice-controlled systems emerging as a popular choice due to their convenience and user-friendly interface. This proposed work aims to develop a Raspberry Pi-integrated AI bot for home automation, enhancing the user experience and functionality of smart homes. The proposed system leverages the capabilities of Raspberry Pi, a versatile single-board computer, to serve as the central hub for home automation. Integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning algorithms, the AI bot enables seamless interaction with various smart devices and appliances within the household. The proposed work begins with the design and implementation of the hardware setup, consisting of Raspberry Pi, compatible sensors, actuators, and communication modules. The software architecture includes developing custom scripts and applications to facilitate communication between the Raspberry Pi and connected devices. Central to the system’s functionality is the implementation of voice recognition and natural language understanding algorithms. These enable users to issue voice commands to the AI bot, which interprets the commands and triggers appropriate actions, such as controlling lights, adjusting room temperature, or managing security systems.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy AHP Approach to Overcome AI Adoption Obstacles in Sustainable Hospitality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers great potential for transforming the hospitality industry, particularly promoting sustainable initiatives. However, several obstacles (barriers) are preventing its widespread implementation. With a focus on sustainability, the current study employs the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (Fuzzy AHP) to assess, rank, and identify these obstacles. This study analyzes the six main barriers that act as obstacles to AI adoption in the hospitality sector: financial, psychological, social, technological and functional, age, and data privacy. To attain this in-depth literature research and expert viewpoints are analyzed. The current study provides guidelines, policies, and recommendations based on the findings, to assist the hospitality industry in adopting AI technology. This research enhances our knowledge of the complex structure underlying AI use in the hospitality sector. This approach provides valuable information for forming sustainable strategies for development in the hospitality industry by expanding the field's expertise.

articleTitle: Retinal Disease Classification in Optical Coherence Tomography Images Using a Convolutional Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) algorithms and deep learning (DL) algorithm applications in ophthalmology are rapidly advancing, particularly in the field of retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) pathology classification. The main goal is to enhance the diagnosis and categorization of retinal diseases, leveraging the capabilities of retinal OCT imaging. This noninvasive technique provides detailed cross-sectional views of the retina using convolutional neural networks (CNN). This imaging method aids in the identification and tracking of various ocular ailments. The integration of ML algorithms in the analysis of retinal OCT images has demonstrated significant potential in early disease detection and classification. Diseases like age-related muscular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, and glaucoma can be more accurately identified and assessed. These algorithms efficiently process retinal OCT images, extracting quantitative data and discerning subtle structural changes and thickness variations that might elude visual inspection. The ML workflow for classifying retinal OCT pathology entails extracting key features from OCT images. These features encompass parameters such as retinal layer thickness, textural attributes, blood vessel characteristics, and anomalies like fluid or exudate. These extracted features, such as logistic regression (LR) and random forest (RF), serve as input for training the ML model. The model's efficacy is then validated on an independent data set to gauge its accuracy and performance, and results are compared with the CNN algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-label Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis using Fuzzy LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: With increase in availability of social media side and cheap cost Internet facility, in present scenario people prefer to share their feelings and emotions in the form of comments or reviews on social media site. These comments are an important source for the reviewers and company people to know about their product from the customer point of view. The reviews mostly contain text words, emojis, number and special characters and thus, before processing the reviews per-processing technique is preferred to removed unwanted information. Many reviewers analyze the reviews into two classes i.e., positive and negative. In this paper, an attempt is made to analyze the reviews on multi scale i.e., in five scales namely great, good, average, bad, very bad. In this work, a combination of two machine learning techniques like LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) and Fuzzy system is used to analyze the reviews. The LSTM is used to classify the reviews in binary class and based on the predicted polarity of the reviews, Fuzzy system helps in predicting the class in the scale of five. As labeled reviews are considered for analysis, the performance of the system is evaluated using confusion matrix and its associated parameters.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Educational Platforms: Bridging Global Learning Divides with DistilBERT for Content Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: AI-powered educational approaches are transforming production by leveraging powerful AI models to create very high-quality educational content, and tailoring learning experiences to the specific needs of students. However, these advances are often hampered by the computational requirements of existing large models, which limit their scalability and accessibility in a wide range of educational settings. To overcome these challenges this review provides a method unique approach to optimizing content development processes while maintaining quality and accessibility. This initiative seeks to streamline the production of educational content, enhance learning processes, and incorporate real-time feedback mechanisms, all of which are essential for the development of global education, happens worldwide bridging learning gaps, and providing an inclusive learning environment for students around the world with 99.5% accuracy. This study focuses on the transformative potential of AI to transform educational approaches, making education more accessible and successful in different socio-economic and geographical contexts.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Predictive Modeling for Accelerated Drug Discovery and Personalized Medicine Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The research investigates how AI-driven predictive modelling can revolutionize personalized medicine and speed up drug discovery. Through the utilization of sophisticated machine learning algorithms and vast biomedical datasets, the research endeavours to expedite the identification of auspicious medication candidates and customize therapies to specific patient profiles. According to the research, AI models considerably improve predictions of drug-target interactions, anticipate side effects, and pinpoint important biomarkers for patient classification. These AI-driven techniques perform better than conventional methods in terms of processing speed and predicted accuracy, which speeds up the process of finding efficient medications and individualized treatment regimens. This research holds the potential to completely transform the pharmaceutical sector by cutting down on the duration and expenses associated with medication development and enhancing patient outcomes via more focused treatments. AI technologies enable a significant improvement in the accuracy and effectiveness of medical treatments; the model shows a 20% increase in accuracy over conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Meta-Learning Strategies for Engineering Education Reform: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks and Reinforcement Learning Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: There are many barriers in the use of technological education like low inclusive learning education resources; better ways of educating students and outcome assessment technology -based teaching and learning approach also poses a challenge in education since traditional teaching designs meet the demands in a way that enhances poor students’ attendance in class as well as poor performance. Inasmuch as the conventional approaches for curriculum development as well as manual grading approaches are rigid and cannot be adapted to other settings. This paper introduces a new meta-learning strategy to enhance a variety of machine learning; convolutional neural networks to network visual learning aids, grading tools, and instructional information to set up learning environments. RL algorithms are used in creating student learning paths or programmers, and smart tutoring systems that adapt with the students’ performance and behavioral characteristics. Briefly, the Meta-learning strategies such as MAML and few-shot learning improve the flexibility of these models and make them capable of Rapid Adaptability to perform new learning tasks with a small amount of data. The approach consists of recognizing educational problems, obtaining and preprocessing data, choosing the suitable CNN and RL models, using meta-learning approaches. Ongoing monitoring and feedback are included with the tools in order to maintain update and modify the tools as needed. Evaluation of the performance shows a substantial enhancement in engagement of students, adoption of learning, and grading with the accuracy of 92% for AAC, precision of 90%, recall of 88%, and f1-score are 89%.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in Photovoltaic System Using Machine Learning Techniques and ANN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Ensuring the reliability of a photovoltaic (PV) system depends on effective fault classification and detection. Under various environmental circumstances, traditional fault detection methods may incorrectly identify operational PV systems as defective or vice versa. This paper proposes a machine learning and artificial neural network (ANN) model for effective fault diagnosis in PV systems. The dataset is pre-processed and fed into multiple models, including SVM, KNN, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, and ANN. This study uses metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score as performance measures. The results show that the ANN can reliably find faults and classify them in a wide range of environmental conditions by using its power to see intricate patterns. The findings show that the proposed model effectively improves fault diagnosis in PV systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Engineering Pedagogy through Deep Learning: Applications of Explainable AI and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Conventional engineering pedagogy frequently fails to deliver individualized learning experiences and places a strong emphasis on one-size-fits-all methods of instruction. Meeting the requirements of every individual student and improving learning outcomes become more challenging as a result. Modern instructional tools, however state-of-the-art, typically cannot offer personalized, data-driven insights. Since many systems are clear, it might be challenging for educators and learners to comprehend the recommendations made. The concept-based transformer network presented in this work is intended to improve the personalized learning experience in engineering education. Using focus, this new neural system focuses on the most relevant elements of a student’s education, providing personalized recommendations and assessments. Transparency is achieved through the inclusion of semantic AI, so that teachers and students can understand and validate the recommendations made by the system The proposed approach begins with the collection of large amounts of data, which including demographic information, contact records, and measures of student performance. Pre-processing assures data accuracy and quality. Personalized learning strategies and recommendations are generated through feedforward neural networks and integrated into the instructional platform. Performance measurement and user feedback for incremental change and continuous monitoring. Key metrics such as student engagement, outcomes for learning, and satisfaction levels are used to assess the effectiveness of the model. A comparison of the proposed model with current methods demonstrates its ability to provide scalable, transparent and customizable learning solutions.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Image Analysis: The Integration of MLP and GRU Architectures in Advanced Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Although there have been significant advances in computer vision recently, there are still difficulties in efficiently interpreting dynamic and complicated visual input. Through the integration of Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) in advanced picture analysis, this study suggests a novel way to overcome these issues. Utilizing the advantages of both systems, the integrated model seeks to improve visual information comprehension and interpretation. Computer vision applications involving temporal context and semantic understanding are sometimes difficult for traditional approaches to handle. MLPs are good at collecting spatial features; on the other hand, GRUs are efficient at processing data sequentially. This research aims to develop and evaluate an integrated MLP-GRU model for advanced image analysis, combining the strengths of MLPs and GRUs. The model aims to achieve superior performance in tasks like object detection, image classification, and semantic segmentation. The model combines MLPs for spatial feature extraction and GRUs for capturing temporal dependencies within sequential data. The experimental results show significant improvements in accuracy of 98%, compared to traditional approaches. The model also demonstrates the ability to discern complex visual patterns and make accurate predictions. This study highlights the potential of hybrid neural network architectures in image analysis, highlighting the paradigm shift in computer vision and their ability to analyze diverse and dynamic visual data.

articleTitle: A Review on Brain Tumor Analysis Using Conventional and Deep Learning Techniques on MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: An abnormal tissue development on the unchecked cell division is known as a brain tumor. Early diagnosis of these conditions may have several benefits, including the ability to discover treatments that can reverse the disease's course and prevent any difficult side effects. One of the main tools used for diagnosis is the magnetic resonance imager (MRI).The MRI images contains too much of data for manual interpretation and analysis. Within the specialty of medical imaging systems, MRI brain tumor segmentation has emerged as a new clinical study focus. Appropriate on-site and off-site surveillance of the tumor's location and size is a godsend for tumor diagnosis. This study is the review on brain tumor analysis using deep learning techniques on MRI images. This study helps the researcher to find the best method. This method also shows that the deep learning is the best method with better accuracy of 79.45% for brain tumor segmentation.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic-Driven Protection Coordination for Robust DFIG System Operation Under Symmetrical Fault Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Ensuring the reliability and stability of Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG)-based wind energy systems during grid disturbances, particularly symmetrical faults, is crucial for modern power systems. Conventional protection techniques such as the Rotor End Series Resistance Crowbar (RESRC), Rotor End Parallel Resistance Crowbar (REPRC), and DC Link Chopper (DLC) have been individually employed to mitigate these disturbances. However, these methods often face challenges, including increased mechanical stress, converter damage, and suboptimal fault ride-through (FRT) capabilities. This paper presents an advanced protection coordination strategy driven by fuzzy logic, designed to integrate and optimize the RESRC, REPRC, and DLC techniques for enhanced system resilience under symmetrical fault conditions. The presented approach not only ensures the continuity of grid operations but also minimizes the risks of overcurrent and overvoltage, thereby extending the operational life of the DFIG system. The fuzzy logic controller dynamically adjusts protection actions based on real-time fault severity, providing a robust, adaptive, and efficient solution for fault management in wind energy systems. MATLAB Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of this coordinated approach in maintaining grid stability and protecting critical components during severe grid disturbances over conventional method.

articleTitle: Visual Safety Monitoring Detecting Deviations in Industrial Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Safety in the work place is essential for protecting workers from workplace accidents and maintaining a safe and efficient workplace culture. Traditional industrial safety monitoring methods are time-consuming and subject to human error. In recent years, industries addresses this issue by utilizing computer vision and marking safety violations in real-time. The proposed system detects safety deviations such as missing safety helmets, vests, and masks, allowing for proactive intervention to avert accidents. Processing live video feeds from CCTV cameras via the Coral dev board with suitable Deep Learning algorithm the proposed system ensures real-time detection of safety violations. In the proposed model, YOLOv8x algorithm is used, it achieves the precision of 0.985, recall of 0.874, and accuracy of 0.893 by utilizing the dataset comprising 2,801 images and videos combined collected from various sources. Also, the proposed system's flexibility in altering detection parameters depending on unique work site requirements makes it applicable to various industrial shop floor and safety regulations. The data visualization dashboard offers real-time notifications. It enhances workplace safety, saves time, and improves operational efficiency by detecting deviations and providing early alerts for safety violations using the powerful algorithms, and seamless communication.

articleTitle: Development and Enhancement of ROS-based SLAM Methods for the Navigation of Wheeled Mobile Robots in Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In recent years, wheeled mobile robotics (WMR) for small and large-scale Industry 4.0 applications are being implemented in warehouses, factories, and smart cities. Mobile robots must navigate constantly changing dynamic environments, which present significant challenges due to the difficulty of real-time mapping, collision avoidance, and path planning optimization. This research develops an autonomous mobile robot (AMR) system capable of navigating independently through unfamiliar and uncharted indoor environments. To achieve this, a sensor system tailored to the environment is used to perform specific tasks. The data collected by these sensors is processed by an enhanced SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) algorithm, which extends SLAM's capabilities and generates pathways to unexplored regions. A simulation environment is created in Gazebo for mobile robot mapping, integrating lidar and odometry data throughout the process. The slip rate of the four-wheel robot's steering is measured in position, leading to improved chassis pose accuracy. Currently, ROS and STM32 communicate, with the ROS chassis node packaged to receive speed commands, provide feedback from odometer data, and process transformations. Based on experiments and simulations, the system accurately maps the environment and performs precise navigation tasks.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Islanding Detection Scheme in PV Grid Tied System by Scalogram Image Based Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The rapid growth of Distributed Generation (DG) is driven by the persistent need for electricity. Over time, nearly all DG sources are sustainable. Islanding is a significant issue that arises when there is an excessive integration of photovoltaic (PV) inverter-based DG sources. Islanding poses a potential risk to both the clients and their equipment. This study presents a novel approach using machine learning (ML) classifiers to detect islanding by categorising images. In order to distinguish between non-islanding and islanding events, images are utilised to generate the histogram of orientated gradient (HOG) features. The scalogram images are obtained from the time-series signal derived from the point of common coupling (PCC). The Histogram of Orientated Gradients (HOG) algorithm is employed to extract the distinctive characteristics from the images. The generated feature vector is then utilised as an input for the ML classifier during both the training and testing phases. The scalogram image is generated by utilising the total harmonics distortion (THD) characteristic of the voltage. We are assessing the efficacy of the ML classifier through the utilisation of 5-fold cross-validation. The classification results demonstrate that employing a ML classifier with the HOG feature for islanding detection when classifying images yields excellent outcomes and low validation error.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement in Grid-Connected Systems using PV Cell Array Current Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance power quality in three-phase grid-connected systems. Our system, which utilizes a monocrystalline PV cell array, significantly differs from conventional methods. It incorporates a Boost Converter, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT), Voltage Source Converter (VSC), current controller, surge filter, non-linear load, and three-phase grid feeding. The Perturb and Observe method in the MPPT algorithm ensures efficient power absorption. The subsequent stages process power, including a proportional-integral (PI) controller and VSC (DC-Link Voltage), delivering stable power to the three-phase grid for various non-linear loads. The model focuses on improving the power factor, ensuring zero voltage regulation, and eliminating harmonics in the AC mains by implementing a current controller and surge filter. Simulations using MATLAB/Simulink modeling demonstrate the corresponding results.

articleTitle: Fractional Order PID Controlled Interleaved KY Converter with Reduced Current Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: In this paper, a novel DC-DC boost converter, namely ILKYC (Interleaved KY converter) is presented. This converter resembles the behaviour of a boost converter by possessing fast source transient response. Since there are four switches present, the switching stress on each switch is minimized. The output current ripple is minimized as well due to the interleaving process. Above all, the principal advantage of the ILKYC over a typical DC-DC boost converter is that the input ripple current is massively minimized due to the interleaving. This not only reduces the stress on the DC power source, but it also improves its lifetime. A thorough description and illustration of the newly proposed ILKYC is presented along with simulation results to showcase the potency of the new converter. The results of PID and FOPID controlled ILKYCS are compared. The response of FOPID controlled ILKYCS is superior to the response of PID controlled ILKYCS.

articleTitle: Smart Remote Physical Therapy: Deep Learning-Based Patient Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This study is centred on the development of a methodology for remote health surveillance of patients undergoing physical therapy, employing pose detection technology. The approach utilizes advanced deep learning algorithms to assess patients’ body positions during physical exercises, offering instantaneous feedback to both patients and therapists. This method of remote monitoring coupled with personalized feedback aims to enhance patient outcomes, decrease healthcare expenditures, and bolster patient engagement. By integrating pose detection technology, the system ensures precise tracking of patients’ advancements, facilitating tailored therapy interventions and optimizing treatment effectiveness.

articleTitle: Comparing Neural Networks and Machine Learning Approaches for Predicting the Severity of Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: Breast cancer poses a significant health threat and ranks as a leading cause of women’s fatalities globally. To tackle this challenge, we need to focus on improving how we find and treat it early. It’s vital to develop accurate ways to diagnose breast cancer in the medical field. While mammography is effective in detecting breast cancer, the use of Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems can further reduce breast cancer mortality rates. Radiologists and doctors use CAD systems to analyze and decide if breast cancer is ‘Benign" or Malignant". But greater research efforts are essential for enhancing our ability to understand and combat breast cancer. In our study, we looked at different computer-based machine learning methods to predict breast cancer severity. We utilized a comprehensive Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset" to evaluate commonly used Supervised machine learning methods and Artificial Neural Network’s(ANN). Our assessment involved calculation of simple metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score to gauge the effectiveness of these methods. The results,that we obtained in this paper, show that machine learning and ANN’s methods have a big potential in diagnosing breast cancer early, giving useful information for early detection and personalized treatment plans. This study helps healthcare providers by guiding them on finding breast cancer early and managing its severity effectively. It also sets the stage for more research to improve how we diagnose breast cancer using other machine learning methods further in future.

articleTitle: A Survey on Federated Learning for IoT Malware Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: The growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) is expanding rapidly. The count of devices being connected to the internet is growing profusely. IoT malware is malicious software that leads to data breaches, and disruption of the device's functionality and even the device. So, the detection of IoT malware is very crucial. Traditionally, centralized approaches are used for IoT malware analysis which can lead to privacy concerns. Among various approaches for IoT malware analysis, the one focused in this paper is Federated Learning (FL). FL is a collaborative approach in which model training takes place on individual devices, the data remains local to the end devices. FL provides many other advantages like data privacy, improved performance, and scalability. We have explored FL as a promising approach to secure IoT systems. We have discussed different FL techniques, their significance in enhancing IoT security, the challenges they face, and potential solutions.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Financial Markets - A CNN-LSTM Approach to Stock Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST)
abstract: This study investigates the use of deep learning methods in financial markets, with a specific emphasis on predicting stock prices.
